DerSimonian--Laird pooled $d_0$ = 0.243 [0.118, 0.368], $I^2 = 0.92$ (Table~\\ref{tab:entry}, Figure~\\ref{fig:entry}).\n\n\\begin{table}[!htbp]\n\\centering\n\\caption{Retained-frontier coefficient ($d_0$) from the conditional-logit model of field entry, by domain group and cohort. The pre-registered verdict is PARTIAL: criterion 5 (volume-matched CI $> 0$) fails.}\n\\label{tab:entry}\n\\small\n\\begin{tabular}{lccc}\n\\toprule\nModel & $d_0$ & 95\\% CI (concept) & LR \\\\\n\\midrule\nDevelopment set & 0.228 & [0.164, 0.291] & 34.5 \\\\\nHeld-out pooled & 0.322 & [0.291, 0.355] & 325.8 \\\\\nPhysical Sciences & 0.148 & [0.078, 0.219] & -- \\\\\nLife \\& Environment & 0.401 & [0.342, 0.460] & -- \\\\\nSocial Sciences & 0.297 & [0.246, 0.348] & -- \\\\\nMath \\& Decision Sci. & 0.065 & [$-$0.109, 0.239] & -- \\\\\n2010--2014 cohort & 0.321 & [0.292, 0.347] & -- \\\\\n\\bottomrule\n\\end{tabular}\n\\end{table}\n\nThe retained-frontier coefficient survives the conventional RCA density ($D_{\\text{rca}}$) and a share-weighted current presence density: adding $d_0$ after both rivals gives LR = 34.5 on DEV, and $D_{\\text{rca}}$ is absorbed once $d_0$ enters. All three specificity tests reject their nulls after Holm correction (retained-label permutation $p = 0.001$; backbone-rewiring $p = 0.004$; node-label $p = 0.003$).\n\nHowever, the pre-registered verdict is PARTIAL. The volume-matched contrast (comparing entry rates of retained versus entered-but-not-retained fields in the same volume cell) is null: $-$0.028 [$-$0.105, +0.046] on held-out data ($-$0.008 on DEV; Holm $p$ = 0.76). The dose response by retention age on held-out data is 0.098 / 0.075 / 0.304, which is not monotone. Under minimum-conditional-probability proximity \\citep{Hidalgo2007} instead of PMI, $d_0 = -0.021$ ($p = 0.012$), while RCA density becomes strong (LR 246). Persistence is therefore confounded with volume, and the result is backbone-specific.\n\n\\textbf{Gateway centrality.} Gateway centrality does not predict field retention: on 27{,}393 held-out episodes, the increment is effectively zero ($\\Delta$AUC $-$0.00001, 95\\% CI [$-$0.0006, +0.0003]).\n\n\\textbf{Breadth decomposition.} On 3{,}188 DEV concepts\\footnote{Code: \\url{https://github.com/ai-inventor-papers/ai-invention-8795ea-concepts-spread-once-adopters-make-them/tree/fork/run_kLBLH5WmvR9Y/round-4/experiment-12}}, the breadth gap between the top and bottom $O_{2r}$ terciles decomposes as: early contact diversity 77.9\\%, frontier advance $-$4.6\\% (broad concepts gain new fields at similar rates), and retention 26.8\\%. The difference between exploration and retention is 0.464 [0.407, 0.528]. On the held-out pool excluding Medicine (variant iv), the contact share is 0.633 [0.537, 0.727] and the difference is 0.504 [0.329, 0.679] ($I^2 = 0.76$). These shares are an accounting identity for the breadth outcome, not causal effects, because breadth and contact diversity share papers.\n\n\\textbf{Diffusion trajectories.} No discrete trajectory typology passes the naming rule. DTW $k$-medoids and HMM-based clustering on state sequences give an adjusted Rand index of 0.222. PCA reveals a continuum: PC1 (38.8\\% of variance) is a breadth axis, PC2 (10.7\\%) is a keep-versus-lose axis. Early openness (OPEN) correlates with PC1 beyond B5 (held-out partial 0.120, $I^2 = 0$) but not with PC2 (partial $-$0.07 to $-$0.11).\n\n\\textbf{Sequence and closure tests.} A home-prominence half-peak vs off-home take-off test finds no signal beyond the mechanical lag (DEV excess $-$0.009 [$-$0.015, $-$0.003], held-out +0.011 [0.005, 0.016]). Intersection-born concepts take off later (HR 0.47 [0.42, 0.54]). A within-concept closure test\\footnote{Code: \\url{https://github.com/ai-inventor-papers/ai-invention-8795ea-concepts-spread-once-adopters-make-them/tree/fork/run_kLBLH5WmvR9Y/round-5/experiment-15}} is null on the development set (density PPML $b = -0.070$ [$-$0.180, 0.040]; OPEN$_{\\text{home}}$ $b = +0.015$ [$-$0.038, 0.069]). On held-out fields, OPEN$_{\\text{home}}$ is opposite-signed ($-$0.079 [$-$0.146, $-$0.013]). Early openness is a between-concept trait, not a within-concept mechanism.\n\n\\begin{figure}[!htbp]\n  \\centering\n  \\includegraphics[width=\\linewidth,height=0.85\\textheight,keepaspectratio]{figures/fig_entry_v0.pdf}\n  \\caption{Retained-frontier coefficient $d_0$ (log-odds of entering a field per SD of relatedness to the off-home fields that currently retain the concept) from the conditional-logit entry model (rung R3, controlling for home relatedness, field size, entered density, own gateway centrality, RCA density $D_{\\mathrm{rca}}$ and volume density $D_{\\mathrm{vol}}$), by unit. Circles with bars show point estimates with 95\\% concept-bootstrap confidence intervals. The light-blue row is the development (DEV) set used for selection. Dark-blue rows are the held-out domain groups and the 2010--14 onset cohort. The black diamond is the DerSimonian--Laird random-effects estimate pooled over the four held-out groups, and its width spans its 95\\% CI. The right column prints each estimate and interval; $n$ is the number of concepts in each unit. The dashed line marks $d_0 = 0$. $d_0$ is positive with a CI excluding zero in all three evaluable held-out groups (Physical Sciences 0.148, Life \\& Env.\\ 0.401, Social Sciences 0.297) and in the cohort (0.321). Math \\& Decision ($n = 165$, excluded as underpowered before the freeze) is null (0.065 [$-$0.110, 0.234]). The pooled estimate is 0.243 [0.118, 0.368] with high heterogeneity ($I^2 = 0.92$). The frozen verdict is nonetheless PARTIAL: the pre-registered volume-matched contrast is null, and the effect is specific to the PMI backbone.}\n  \\label{fig:entry}\n\\end{figure}\n\n\\subsubsection{Discussion of RQ2}\n\nThe retained-frontier result extends the principle of relatedness to concept adoption. The positive coefficient is large and consistent across three of three evaluable groups, but the PARTIAL verdict limits its interpretation: we cannot fully separate persistence from sustained volume as a predictor of field entry. The effect is also backbone-specific: it holds on the sparse PMI backbone but not under the standard Hidalgo proximity. The breadth decomposition shows that integrating and localised concepts differ primarily in how many fields they contact early, not in how many more fields they enter later. The null closure test and opposite-signed held-out result indicate that openness does not operate as a within-concept mechanism driving diffusion.\n\n\n\\subsection{Confound analysis}\n\\label{sec:confound}\n\nThe openness signal could be an artefact of small yearly samples or of dynamic churn. We tested four null models\\footnote{Code: \\url{https://github.com/ai-inventor-papers/ai-invention-8795ea-concepts-spread-once-adopters-make-them/tree/fork/run_kLBLH5WmvR9Y/round-5/experiment-16}}:\n\n\\textbf{Fixed-size rarefaction.} Subsampling to 10 home papers per year retains 68\\% of the pooled association. The bias-corrected Chao estimator retains 91\\%.\n\n\\textbf{Within-concept permutation null.} The excess churn over a 200-draw within-concept year-label permutation null is indistinguishable from zero: excess NOVCHURN pooled PSP = +0.008 [$-$0.02, +0.03], compared to raw NOVCHURN = +0.116 [+0.09, +0.14]. The $R^2$ of raw persistence on the permutation-null mean is 0.66. What predicts breadth is a static property of the concept's home-topic partner mix.\n\n\\textbf{Degree-preserving configuration null.} Replacing raw ego density and persistence by curveball configuration $z$-scores raises OPEN$_{\\text{home}}$ from +0.092 to +0.115.\n\n\\textbf{Reliability.} Split-half reliability of NOVCHURN$_{\\text{raw}}$ is 0.48. The temporal-excess variants (V2) have split-half Spearman--Brown reliability of approximately 0.01--0.05, and the planted-churn check fails. The disattenuated pooled NOVCHURN PSP is 0.178 [0.141, 0.214] (approximate, CI not independently re-derived).\n\nBecause the V2 temporal-excess measure is unreliable, the analysis cannot adjudicate temporal churn at typical sample sizes ($\\sim$10 home papers/year). The association that survives behaves like a static dispersion property. Temporal turnover is untested rather than refuted.\n\n\\textbf{Partner decomposition.} The home-only signal is carried by partners from new Leiden communities arriving through mixed-field papers: contrast $C_2$ = +0.102 [+0.069, +0.133] (Holm $p$ = 0.0025), domain Shapley $\\phi$ = +0.132 on the cohort (method = +0.012). Controlling for the share of early bridging papers halves NOVCHURN from 0.118 to 0.056.\n\n\n\\subsection{Exploratory AI-domain stage}\n\nAn exploratory retrospective atlas of 37 AI and computer science concepts was constructed from the large panel, examining how concepts such as deep learning, reinforcement learning and generative adversarial networks evolved through the co-occurrence network before their cross-field diffusion. This atlas is outcome-selected and retrospective; it provides qualitative context but no hypothesis-testing power.\n\n\n\\subsection{Representative case studies}\n\nSeven matched case-study pairs were drawn from the breadth decomposition analysis (Table~\\ref{tab:cases}; one pair is shown in Figure~\\ref{fig:case_study}). These pairs are illustration only; all are descriptive with no $p$-value.\n\n\\begin{table}[!htbp]\n\\centering\n\\caption{Representative matched case-study pairs, contrasting high-breadth and low-breadth concepts matched on early volume. All pairs are illustration; no inferential claim is made.}\n\\label{tab:cases}\n\\small\n\\begin{tabular}{lll}\n\\toprule\nHigh-breadth concept & Low-breadth concept & Group \\\\\n\\midrule\nGraphics processing unit & Vertical-axis wind turbine & Eng \\\\\nShotgun proteomics & Image-guided radiation therapy & BGM \\\\\nNanocarriers & Nanosheet & CS \\\\\nSoft power & Autonomous learning & SOC \\\\\nScopus & Oxygen reduction reaction & CS \\\\\nSclerostin & IgG4-related disease & BGM \\\\\nUser-generated content & Mindfulness-based cognitive therapy & SOC \\\\\n\\bottomrule\n\\end{tabular}\n\\end{table}\n\n\\begin{figure}[!htbp]\n  \\centering\n  \\includegraphics[width=\\linewidth,height=0.85\\textheight,keepaspectratio]{figures/fig_case_study_v0.pdf}\n  \\caption{Illustrative matched case-study pair (pair 1 of 7): graphics processing unit (GPU; onset $t_0=2008$, high early-neighbourhood openness OPEN) versus vertical-axis wind turbine (VAWT; $t_0=2009$, low OPEN). Both have an Engineering home field and are matched on early volume and growth. (a) Number of off-home venue fields each concept has ever entered (solid line, filled markers) and currently retains (dashed line, open markers) in each year from $t_0$ to $t_0+8$; GPU is shown in black and VAWT in grey on a shared axis. (b,~c) Topic co-occurrence ego networks over the first three years ($t_0$ to $t_0+2$, all papers). The nodes are the concept's positive-PMI neighbour topics (the concept itself is not drawn), the edges are links between those topics in the topic backbone, node area scales with the number of the concept's papers carrying the topic, and colour gives the topic's Leiden community, named by the plurality OpenAlex field. GPU's neighbourhood has 34 topics in 8 communities (density 0.30). VAWT's has 12 topics in a single Engineering community (density 0.70). The pair illustrates the openness--breadth association and is not evidence for it.}\n  \\label{fig:case_study}\n\\end{figure}\n\n\n\\subsection{Dead ends and negative results}\n\\label{sec:dead_ends}\n\nTable~\\ref{tab:deadends} lists the principal hypotheses and candidate signals that were tested and did not survive.\n\n\\begin{table}[!htbp]\n\\centering\n\\caption{Principal dead ends and negative results.}\n\\label{tab:deadends}\n\\small\n\\begin{tabular}{p{4.2cm}p{2.5cm}p{5.5cm}}\n\\toprule\nHypothesis / candidate & Decisive test & Result \\\\\n\\midrule\nNaturalisation gap ($A^*_h$) & Exp.\\ 1 & Fails every clause ($-$0.006) \\\\\n$D_{\\text{ratio}}$, $F_{\\text{res}}$ & Exp.\\ 3 & No candidate survives \\\\\nGateway landing on $O_{2r}$ & Exp.\\ 4, 5 & $\\Delta$AUC $-$0.00001 held-out \\\\\nH3 gateway-weighted landing & Exp.\\ 5 & Pooled CI includes 0 [$-$0.006, 0.065] \\\\\nOrdering (central-first) & Exp.\\ 6, Eval.\\ 2 & MIXED: 32.6\\% of broad concepts; negative lead-lag; pre-trend \\\\\nTwo discrete trajectory classes & Exp.\\ 6, 12 & HMM-vs-DTW ARI 0.094/0.222 \\\\\nAbandonment penalty ($d_{\\text{lost}}$) & Exp.\\ 7 & Specification-dependent: A1 $-$0.007, R4 +0.064, min-cp $-$0.030 \\\\\nVolume-matched retained-frontier contrast & Exp.\\ 7 & Null: $-$0.028 [$-$0.105, +0.046] held-out \\\\\n$O_5$ external recognition & Exp.\\ 8, Eval.\\ 2 & No indicator beats B5 + onset year \\\\\nRescue and relay models & Exp.\\ 6 & Not supported \\\\\nWithin-concept closure & Exp.\\ 11, 15C & Null on DEV; opposite-signed held-out ($-$0.079) \\\\\n$n_{\\text{authors\\_early}}$ for $O_3$ & Exp.\\ 8, 10 & Non-replication on fresh cohort (+0.014) \\\\\nRETENTION\\_RATIO at R2/R3 & Exp.\\ 10 & Null on cohort ($-$0.043 [$-$0.116, 0.031]) \\\\\nTrait prediction ($P$-B1) & Exp.\\ 15B & Fails: yearly OPEN$_{\\text{home}}$ ICC 0.34--0.39 \\\\\nVocab-free Cheng reversal & Exp.\\ 13 & Not confirmed ($-$0.064 [$-$0.159, 0.031]) \\\\\nCo-author candidate S & Exp.\\ 8 & Computed; not confirmed for any outcome \\\\\n\\bottomrule\n\\end{tabular}\n\\end{table}\n\n\n\\section{Discussion}\n\\label{sec:discussion}\n\n\\subsection{What the openness index captures}\n\nThe OPEN index captures the degree to which a concept's early neighbourhood acquires partners from diverse communities rather than reinforcing existing ones. The signal is not demonstrably temporal turnover but a static topical-dispersion property. A within-concept permutation null absorbs the year-to-year component, yet the association persists: concepts whose home-field co-occurrence partners span many communities tend to reach more fields later. This is consistent with \\citeauthor{March1991}'s (\\citeyear{March1991}) exploration--exploitation distinction at the concept level. However, the within-concept closure test is null on DEV and opposite-signed on held-out fields, indicating that openness operates as a between-concept trait rather than as a within-concept causal mechanism.\n\nThe home-only signal (OPEN$_{\\text{home}}$) is marginal. The stronger OPEN$_{\\text{all}}$ signal is partly mechanically coupled: early off-home papers that enter the ego network are a subset of the papers that determine the outcome. OPEN$_{\\text{sizematch}}$ controls for this coupling and remains significant.\n\n\\subsection{Reconciling consistency and breadth}\n\n\\citet{Cheng2023} found that ideational consistency predicts a concept becoming ``core.'' We replicate their result for volume (+53\\%/SD) but show that, net of volume, the same property predicts \\emph{narrower} cross-field reach. The reversal holds in all five field groups ($I^2 = 0$) and replicates on a fresh cohort. The features predictive of local consolidation and growth are distinct from, and partly opposed to, the features predictive of broad disciplinary spread.\n\n\\subsection{The retained-frontier claim}\n\nThe confirmed field-entry result ($d_0 = 0.322$ on the independent frame) extends the principle of relatedness from economic geography \\citep{Hidalgo2007,Boschma2015} to concept adoption. The result is PARTIAL: the volume-matched contrast is null, and the effect is backbone-specific (it reverses under minimum-conditional-probability proximity). What survives is a PMI-backbone relative-odds effect that cannot be separated from volume. The $I^2$ of 0.92 indicates substantial cross-domain heterogeneity, with Life \\& Environment showing the strongest signal and Mathematics \\& Decision Sciences null.\n\n\\subsection{Limitations}\n\n\\textbf{Effect size.} The OPEN--breadth association is modest. OPEN$_{\\text{home}}$ adds no forecasting gain over B5 (+0.002 [$-$0.003, +0.008]).\n\n\\textbf{Measurement noise.} Split-half reliability of OPEN$_{\\text{home}}$ is 0.49. The temporal-excess variants have split-half reliability below 0.05, so temporal versus static dispersion cannot be resolved at available sample sizes.\n\n\\textbf{Vocabulary bias.} The legacy OpenAlex concept vocabulary is survivor-selected. Frame~N is small (636 concepts) with pre-unseal power of 0.47.\n\n\\textbf{Coupling.} About half of the OPEN$_{\\text{all}}$ signal is mechanical coupling between the ego-network construction (which uses off-home papers) and the breadth outcome. OPEN$_{\\text{home}}$ is free of this coupling but marginal.\n\n\\textbf{Domain heterogeneity.} Life \\& Environment shows the weakest OPEN signal (PSP +0.042). The retained-field relatedness $I^2$ is 0.92.\n\n\\textbf{Not causal.} Early ego-network openness could reflect a concept's intrinsic generality, the diversity of the research community around it, or the breadth of the problems it addresses.\n\n\\textbf{Prior unsealing.} Held-out outcomes were previously unsealed by two earlier experiments in the same project, so the indicator-screen held-out results are robustness checks.\n\n\n\\section{Conclusions}\n\\label{sec:conclusions}\n\nWe screened 53 early temporal network indicators for predicting the cross-disciplinary breadth of new scientific concepts, using 12{,}499 concepts from the OpenAlex corpus with held-out validation and a fresh cohort confirmation. Seven indicators are confirmed, composing into the OPEN index that captures topical non-redundancy in a concept's early co-occurrence neighbourhood. The signal is a static between-concept trait; temporal turnover could not be tested at available sample sizes. Early openness predicts breadth; early consolidation predicts volume but not breadth. Concepts spread next to fields related to those currently retaining them, but the pre-registered verdict is PARTIAL: persistence and volume are confounded, and the effect is backbone-specific.\n\n\n\\section*{Declarations}\n\n\\subsection*{Funding}\nNot applicable.\n\n\\subsection*{Conflict of interest}\nThe authors declare no conflict of interest.\n\n\\subsection*{Availability of data and materials}\nThe study uses the publicly available OpenAlex bulk snapshot (2026-09-23). Concept frames, indicator matrices and analysis scripts are available from the corresponding author upon request.\n\n\\subsection*{Code availability}\nAnalysis code is available from the corresponding author upon request.\n\n\\subsection*{Authors' contributions}\nAll authors contributed to the study design, analysis and manuscript preparation.\n\n\\bibliographystyle{plainnat}\n\\bibliography{references}\n\n\\end{document}", "stderr": "", "interrupted": false, "isImage": false, "noOutputExpected": false}

for k, v in es["pools"].items():

/* stepper */
.steps{display:flex;flex-wrap:wrap;gap:6px;list-style:none;padding:0;margin:10px 0}
.steps button{min-height:42px;min-width:42px;border:1.5px solid #b9c0c8;background:#fff;border-radius:8px;padding:6px 11px;font:inherit;font-size:.88rem;color:var(--ink2);cursor:pointer}
.steps button[aria-current="step"]{background:var(--accent);border-color:var(--accent);color:#fff}
.stepnav{display:flex;gap:10px;align-items:center;margin:12px 0}
.stepnav button{min-height:44px;min-width:44px;padding:8px 16px;border-radius:8px;border:1.5px solid var(--accent);background:#fff;color:var(--accent);font:inherit;font-weight:600;cursor:pointer}
.stepnav button:disabled{opacity:.38;cursor:not-allowed}
.stage{display:grid;grid-template-columns:minmax(0,1fr) minmax(0,1fr) minmax(0,1fr);gap:14px;margin-top:10px}
@media (max-width:860px){.stage{grid-template-columns:minmax(0,1fr)}}
.stage .box{border:1px solid var(--rule);border-radius:8px;padding:12px 14px;background:#fcfcfd}
.stage .box h4{margin-bottom:6px}
.why{margin-top:12px;font-size:.97rem;color:var(--ink2)}
table{border-collapse:collapse;width:100%;font-size:.9rem}
th,td{text-align:left;padding:5px 8px;border-bottom:1px solid var(--rule);vertical-align:top}
th{font-weight:650;color:var(--ink2);font-size:.82rem}
td.num,th.num{text-align:right;font-variant-numeric:tabular-nums}
.tscroll{overflow-x:auto;max-width:100%}
.pill{display:inline-block;font-size:.76rem;padding:1px 8px;border-radius:20px;background:var(--base-soft);color:var(--ink2);white-space:nowrap}
.pill.ok{background:#e3f3ea;color:var(--ok)} .pill.bad{background:var(--fail-soft);color:var(--fail)} .pill.acc{background:var(--accent-soft);color:var(--accent)}
figure{margin:18px 0}
figure img{max-width:100%;height:auto;display:block;border:1px solid var(--rule);border-radius:6px;background:#fff}
figcaption{font-size:.86rem;color:var(--ink2);margin-top:8px;max-width:80ch}
/* browser */
.browser{display:grid;grid-template-columns:minmax(0,5fr) minmax(0,6fr);gap:18px}
@media (max-width:900px){.browser{grid-template-columns:minmax(0,1fr)}}
.list{list-style:none;margin:0;padding:0;max-height:430px;overflow-y:auto;border:1px solid var(--rule);border-radius:8px}
.list li{border-bottom:1px solid var(--rule)}
.list button{display:flex;justify-content:space-between;gap:10px;width:100%;text-align:left;border:0;background:#fff;padding:9px 12px;min-height:44px;font:inherit;font-size:.9rem;color:var(--ink);cursor:pointer}
.list button[aria-pressed="true"]{background:var(--accent-soft);box-shadow:inset 4px 0 0 var(--accent)}
.list .meta{color:var(--muted);font-size:.8rem;white-space:nowrap}
.detail{border:1px solid var(--rule);border-radius:8px;padding:14px;background:#fcfcfd}
.cmp{display:grid;grid-template-columns:repeat(3,minmax(0,1fr));gap:10px;margin:10px 0}
.cmp div{border-radius:8px;padding:10px;text-align:center;border:1px solid var(--rule);background:#fff}
.cmp .v{font-size:1.5rem;font-weight:700;font-variant-numeric:tabular-nums}
.cmp .l{font-size:.78rem;color:var(--muted);line-height:1.3}
.cmp .base .v{color:var(--base)} .cmp .meth .v{color:var(--accent)}
.count{font-size:.9rem;color:var(--ink2);margin:6px 0}
.term{font:inherit;font-size:inherit;color:inherit;background:none;border:0;padding:0 1px;margin:0;border-bottom:1.5px dotted var(--accent);cursor:help;line-height:inherit;min-height:0}
.tip{position:fixed;z-index:70;max-width:330px;background:#fff;color:var(--ink);border:1px solid #b9c0c8;box-shadow:0 6px 20px rgba(0,0,0,.14);border-radius:8px;padding:10px 12px;font-size:.88rem;line-height:1.5;font-weight:400;text-align:left}
.tip[hidden]{display:none}
.tip strong{display:block;margin-bottom:2px}
dl.gloss{display:grid;grid-template-columns:minmax(0,1fr);gap:0}
dl.gloss dt{font-weight:650;margin-top:10px}
dl.gloss dd{margin:2px 0 0;color:var(--ink2);font-size:.95rem}
footer{padding:36px 0 60px;background:var(--panel)}
footer h2{font-size:1.3rem;margin-top:24px}
footer ul{padding-left:1.2rem}
.cols2{columns:2 340px;column-gap:40px}
.cols2 dt,.cols2 dd{break-inside:avoid}
.statusline{font-size:.9rem;color:var(--ink2)}
.match{font-weight:650}
.match.yes{color:var(--ok)} .match.no{color:var(--fail)}
.sr{position:absolute;width:1px;height:1px;overflow:hidden;clip:rect(0 0 0 0);white-space:nowrap}
.limits li{margin-bottom:.5rem}
code{font-family:var(--mono);font-size:.88em;background:#f1f2f4;padding:1px 4px;border-radius:4px}
</style>
</head>
<body>
<a class="skip" href="#main">Skip to main content</a>
<header class="top">
  <div class="wrap">
    <p class="small" style="margin:0 0 .4rem">Interactive companion to the paper</p>
    <h1>Early co-occurrence network openness predicts cross-disciplinary concept breadth: evidence from 12,499 scientific concepts</h1>
    <p class="authors">AI Inventor</p>
    <div class="links">
      <a class="btn primary" href="https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/gh/ai-inventor-papers/ai-invention-8795ea-concepts-spread-once-adopters-make-them@fork/run_kLBLH5WmvR9Y/paper.pdf">Read the paper (PDF)</a>
      <a class="btn" href="https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/gh/ai-inventor-papers/ai-invention-8795ea-concepts-spread-once-adopters-make-them@fork/run_kLBLH5WmvR9Y/report.pdf">Read the full research report</a>
      <a class="btn" href="https://github.com/ai-inventor-papers/ai-invention-8795ea-concepts-spread-once-adopters-make-them/tree/fork/run_kLBLH5WmvR9Y">Code repository</a>
    </div>
  </div>
</header>
<nav class="sections" aria-label="Page sections">
  <ul>
    <li><a href="#finding">The finding</a></li>
    <li><a href="#how">How it works</a></li>
    <li><a href="#evidence">Explore the evidence</a></li>
    <li><a href="#try">Try it</a></li>
    <li><a href="#fails">Where it fails</a></li>
    <li><a href="#notes">Links, data, glossary</a></li>
  </ul>
</nav>
<main id="main">

<!-- ============ 1. FINDING ============ -->
<section class="block" id="finding" aria-labelledby="h-finding">
<div class="wrap">
  <h2 id="h-finding">The finding</h2>
  <div class="grid2">
    <div class="prose">
      <p class="q">Which early signals in a concept's topic network tell us whether it will later spread across many fields?</p>
      <p>Popularity already explains a lot. A five-feature <button type="button" class="term" data-term="B5">popularity baseline</button> reaches Spearman 0.65–0.86 with later breadth, so any network signal has to add something beyond it. The paper screens 53 early indicators and composes the survivors into the <button type="button" class="term" data-term="OPEN">OPEN index</button>: a concept's early tendency to acquire novel, community-spanning co-occurrence partners.</p>
      <p>Measured on the concept's home field only, and net of the baseline, OPEN has the same sign in every body of data that was not used to choose it:</p>
      <div class="bignum" id="big-num" aria-describedby="big-ci"></div>
      <div class="bignum-ci" id="big-ci"></div>
      <p>The association is small, and the pool is descriptive: all non-selection bodies except the 2015–17 cohort had outcomes read in earlier analyses. It adds almost nothing to a forecast. What it shows is a consistent direction: concepts whose early partners span more topic communities reach more fields later.</p>
    </div>
    <div class="view" style="margin-top:0">
      <p class="q">Does the association hold in every body of data?</p>
      <p class="small" style="margin:0">Each row is one body of concepts. The value is the <button type="button" class="term" data-term="PSP">partial Spearman</button> of the index with <button type="button" class="term" data-term="O2r">rarefied breadth</button>, after removing what the baseline explains.</p>
      <div class="controls">
        <fieldset><legend>Index</legend><div class="seg" role="radiogroup" aria-label="Index">
          <label><input type="radio" name="f-feat" value="OPEN_home" checked><span>OPEN<sub>home</sub></span></label>
          <label><input type="radio" name="f-feat" value="NOVCHURN_home"><span>NOVCHURN<sub>home</sub></span></label>
        </div></fieldset>
        <fieldset><legend>Control rung</legend><div class="seg" role="radiogroup" aria-label="Control rung">
          <label><input type="radio" name="f-rung" value="R0"><span>R0</span></label>
          <label><input type="radio" name="f-rung" value="R2" checked><span>R2</span></label>
          <label><input type="radio" name="f-rung" value="R3"><span>R3</span></label>
        </div></fieldset>
        <label class="check"><input type="checkbox" id="f-dev" checked> Show the selection body</label>
      </div>
      <div class="legend" aria-hidden="true">
        <span><i class="sw-sq"></i>Non-selection body, 95% CI</span>
        <span><i class="sw-dev"></i>Selection body (not pooled)</span>
        <span><i class="sw-band"></i>Shuffled-feature 95th percentile</span>
        <span><i class="sw-dia"></i>DerSimonian–Laird pool</span>
      </div>
      <div class="chart" id="chart-finding"></div>
      <p class="small" id="finding-rungnote"></p>
      <p class="takeaway" id="take-finding" aria-live="polite"></p>
    </div>
  </div>
</div>
</section>

<!-- ============ 2. HOW IT WORKS ============ -->
<section class="block" id="how" aria-labelledby="h-how">
<div class="wrap">
  <h2 id="h-how">How it works</h2>
  <div class="prose">
    <p class="q">What does the method do to one concept, from raw papers to a pooled estimate?</p>
    <p>Follow the graphics processing unit (GPU) through the six stages, with its matched partner, the vertical-axis wind turbine (VAWT), beside it. Both have an Engineering home and were matched on early volume and growth before their outcomes were looked at. Every value below is the one the run recorded for them.</p>
  </div>
  <div class="view" id="stepper" tabindex="-1" aria-roledescription="stepper">
    <div class="chart" id="pipeline" aria-hidden="true"></div>
    <ol class="steps" id="step-markers" aria-label="Stages"></ol>
    <div class="stepnav">
      <button type="button" id="step-prev">&larr; Previous</button>
      <button type="button" id="step-next">Next &rarr;</button>
      <span class="small">Left and right arrow keys also move between stages.</span>
    </div>
    <div id="step-live" class="sr" aria-live="polite"></div>
    <h3 id="step-title"></h3>
    <div class="stage">
      <div class="box"><h4>What goes in</h4><div id="step-in"></div></div>
      <div class="box"><h4>What is done</h4><div id="step-do"></div></div>
      <div class="box"><h4>What comes out</h4><div id="step-out"></div></div>
    </div>
    <p class="why" id="step-why"></p>
    <figure id="step-fig" hidden>
      <img src="figures/fig_case_study_v0.png" alt="Three panels. Left: step lines of off-home fields entered and retained by year since onset; GPU climbs to 11 entered and 8 retained by year 8, VAWT to 6 and 4. Middle: GPU's early ego network, 34 topic nodes in 8 coloured communities, loosely connected. Right: VAWT's ego network, 12 nodes all in one Engineering community, tightly connected." loading="lazy" width="1300" height="560">
      <figcaption>Illustrative matched case-study pair from Experiment 12 (case pair 1 of 7): graphics processing unit (GPU; onset t<sub>0</sub>=2008, high early-neighbourhood openness OPEN) versus vertical-axis wind turbine (VAWT; t<sub>0</sub>=2009, low OPEN). Both have an Engineering home field and are matched on early volume and growth. (a) Number of off-home venue fields each concept has ever entered (solid line, filled markers) and currently retains (dashed line, open markers) in each year from t<sub>0</sub> to t<sub>0</sub>+8. (b, c) Topic co-occurrence ego networks over the first three years (t<sub>0</sub> to t<sub>0</sub>+2, all papers); colour gives the topic's Leiden community. GPU's neighbourhood has 34 topics in 8 communities (density 0.30). VAWT's has 12 topics in a single Engineering community (density 0.70). The pair illustrates the openness–breadth association and is not evidence for it.</figcaption>
    </figure>
  </div>
  <figure>
    <img src="figures/fig_overview_v0.jpg" alt="Study design flow: OpenAlex snapshot (476M works) to concept identification (56,643 legacy concepts, 12,499 grounded), to a panel split (DEV 4,771; held-out 3,372; cohort 4,356; fresh cohort 1,443), to 53 indicators in six families, feeding RQ1 screen and validate (7 confirmed, OPEN pooled +0.069) and, separately, RQ2 conditional logit (11,841 concepts, d0 = 0.322, verdict PARTIAL)." loading="lazy" width="2000" height="858">
    <figcaption>Overview of the study design, read left to right. The OpenAlex snapshot (476M works, 129.4M base works 1995–2022) is title-matched against 56,643 legacy concepts, and Aho–Corasick matching plus an LLM precision gate keeps 12,499 grounded concepts. The panel split assigns these to a development set (DEV 4,771), four held-out domain groups (3,372) and a 2010–2014 onset cohort (4,356). A fresh 2015–2017 cohort (1,443) comes from a separate scan. For each concept, 53 early indicators in six families are computed in the t<sub>0</sub> to t<sub>0</sub>+2 window, screened on DEV and validated on held-out groups (RQ1). Separately, a conditional-logit entry model is fitted on an independent frame of 11,841 concepts (RQ2).</figcaption>
  </figure>
</div>
</section>

<!-- ============ 3. EVIDENCE ============ -->
<section class="block" id="evidence" aria-labelledby="h-evidence">
<div class="wrap">
  <h2 id="h-evidence">Explore the evidence</h2>

  <div class="view" id="v-screen">
    <p class="q">Which of the frozen early indicators survive testing on held-out fields?</p>
    <p class="small" style="margin:0">The 10 indicators ranked highest on DEV, each tested once on four held-out field groups and two cohort splits. Confirmation needs Holm-corrected p &lt; 0.05 and a pooled 95% CI that excludes zero.</p>
    <div class="controls">
      <label><span class="clabel">Show estimate for</span>
        <select id="s-unit">
          <option value="pooled">DerSimonian–Laird pool (6 units)</option>
          <option value="PHYS">Physical Sciences</option>
          <option value="LIFEENV">Life &amp; Environment</option>
          <option value="SOC">Social Sciences</option>
          <option value="MATHDEC">Math &amp; Decision</option>
          <option value="COH_DEVHOME">2010–14 cohort, DEV homes</option>
          <option value="COH_OTHER">2010–14 cohort, other homes</option>
        </select></label>
      <label><span class="clabel">Order</span>
        <select id="s-sort"><option value="est">By estimate</option><option value="abs">By size, ignoring sign</option><option value="fam">By family</option></select></label>
      <label class="check"><input type="checkbox" id="s-conf"> Confirmed only</label>
    </div>
    <div class="legend" aria-hidden="true"><span><i class="sw-sq"></i>Confirmed</span><span><i class="sw-dev"></i>Not confirmed</span></div>
    <div class="chart" id="chart-screen"></div>
    <p class="takeaway" id="take-screen" aria-live="polite"></p>
  </div>

  <div class="view" id="v-browser">
    <p class="q">What does OPEN change for one concept's forecast?</p>
    <p class="small" style="margin:0">All 1,443 concepts of the fresh 2015–2017 cohort, the one body never used in any earlier step. For each, the run recorded two frozen forecasts of breadth fitted on the earlier frame: the baseline (B5 only) and B5 plus OPEN<sub>home</sub>. The chart plots every concept with an observed outcome: OPEN<sub>home</sub> against how far the observed breadth sits above or below the baseline forecast. Click a point or a list row.</p>
    <div class="controls">
      <label><span class="clabel">Search</span><input type="search" id="b-q" placeholder="Concept name" aria-label="Search concepts by name"></label>
      <label><span class="clabel">Home group</span><select id="b-group"><option value="">All groups</option></select></label>
      <label><span class="clabel">Concept type</span><select id="b-type"><option value="">All types</option></select></label>
      <label><span class="clabel">Sort list by</span><select id="b-sort">
        <option value="open">OPEN<sub>home</sub>, high to low</option>
        <option value="gain">OPEN helped most</option>
        <option value="hurt">OPEN hurt most</option>
        <option value="y">Observed breadth, high to low</option>
        <option value="name">Name</option></select></label>
      <label class="check"><input type="checkbox" id="b-obs" checked> Only concepts with an observed outcome</label>
      <label class="check"><input type="checkbox" id="b-fail"> Only cases where OPEN moved the forecast away</label>
    </div>
    <p class="count" id="b-count" aria-live="polite"></p>
    <div class="legend" aria-hidden="true"><span><i class="sw-dev" style="border-radius:50%"></i>Concept</span><span><i class="sw-fail"></i>OPEN moved forecast away from observed</span><span><i class="sw-sq" style="border-radius:50%"></i>Selected</span></div>
    <div class="chart" id="chart-scatter" tabindex="0" role="img" aria-label="Scatter of OPEN home against observed breadth minus baseline forecast. Use left and right arrow keys to move the selection through points."></div>
    <div class="browser" style="margin-top:14px">
      <div><ul class="list" id="b-list" aria-label="Concepts"></ul><p class="small" id="b-more"></p></div>
      <div class="detail" id="b-detail" aria-live="polite"></div>
    </div>
    <p class="takeaway" id="take-browser" aria-live="polite"></p>
  </div>

  <div class="view" id="v-entry">
    <p class="q">Does a concept next enter fields related to the fields that currently keep it?</p>
    <p class="small" style="margin:0">A separate question on an independent frame of 11,841 concepts. The <button type="button" class="term" data-term="condlogit">conditional logit</button> asks which field a concept enters next; <button type="button" class="term" data-term="d0">d<sub>0</sub></button> is the extra log-odds per SD of relatedness to the <button type="button" class="term" data-term="retaining">retaining fields</button>, after home relatedness, field size, entered density, own gateway centrality, RCA density and volume density.</p>
    <div class="controls">
      <label class="check"><input type="checkbox" id="e-dev" checked> Show DEV (selection data)</label>
      <label class="check"><input type="checkbox" id="e-pool" checked> Show held-out pool</label>
    </div>
    <div class="legend" aria-hidden="true"><span><i class="sw-sq" style="border-radius:50%"></i>Held-out unit, 95% concept-bootstrap CI</span><span><i class="sw-dev" style="border-radius:50%"></i>DEV</span><span><i class="sw-dia"></i>DerSimonian–Laird pool, 4 held-out groups</span></div>
    <div class="chart" id="chart-entry"></div>
    <p class="takeaway" id="take-entry" aria-live="polite"></p>
  </div>

  <div class="view" id="v-cheng">
    <p class="q">If an open neighbourhood goes with breadth, does a stable one go with growth?</p>
    <p class="small" style="margin:0">The paper rebuilt Cheng et al.'s <button type="button" class="term" data-term="consistency">ideational consistency</button> for 12,311 concepts. Bars start at zero; whiskers are 95% concept-bootstrap CIs.</p>
    <div class="controls">
      <fieldset><legend>View</legend><div class="seg" role="radiogroup" aria-label="Consistency view">
        <label><input type="radio" name="c-view" value="out" checked><span>By outcome</span></label>
        <label><input type="radio" name="c-view" value="grp"><span>Reach, by field group</span></label>
      </div></fieldset>
    </div>
    <div class="chart" id="chart-cheng"></div>
    <p class="takeaway" id="take-cheng" aria-live="polite"></p>
  </div>
</div>
</section>

<!-- ============ 4. TRY IT ============ -->
<section class="block" id="try" aria-labelledby="h-try">
<div class="wrap">
  <h2 id="h-try">Try it</h2>
  <div class="view" id="v-calc">
    <p class="q">Can I compute OPEN myself and get the recorded value?</p>
    <p class="small" style="margin:0">The index is simple enough to run here exactly. Each of the six components is z-scored with the constants frozen over all 12,499 frame concepts, signed (density and persistence count against openness), and averaged when at least 4 of 6 are present. Pick one of the 14 case-study concepts and a build; untick components to see how much each carries.</p>
    <div class="controls">
      <label><span class="clabel">Concept</span><select id="k-concept"></select></label>
      <fieldset><legend>Build</legend><div class="seg" role="radiogroup" aria-label="Build">
        <label><input type="radio" name="k-build" value="home" checked><span>Home only</span></label>
        <label><input type="radio" name="k-build" value="all"><span>All papers</span></label>
        <label><input type="radio" name="k-build" value="size"><span>Size-matched</span></label>
      </div></fieldset>
    </div>
    <fieldset><legend>Components used</legend><div class="controls" id="k-comps" style="margin-top:0"></div></fieldset>
    <div class="grid2" style="grid-template-columns:minmax(0,6fr) minmax(0,5fr)">
      <div class="tscroll"><table id="k-table"><caption class="sr">OPEN computation for the selected concept</caption><thead><tr><th scope="col">Component</th><th scope="col" class="num">Recorded</th><th scope="col" class="num">Mean</th><th scope="col" class="num">SD</th><th scope="col" class="num">Signed z</th></tr></thead><tbody></tbody></table></div>
      <div><div class="chart" id="chart-calc"></div></div>
    </div>
    <p class="statusline" id="k-status" aria-live="polite"></p>
    <p class="takeaway" id="take-calc" aria-live="polite"></p>
  </div>

  <div class="view" id="v-sweep">
    <p class="q">Does OPEN improve the forecast for the most open concepts?</p>
    <p class="small" style="margin:0">Over the 573 cohort concepts that have both forecasts and an observed outcome, keep only those at or above a percentile of OPEN<sub>home</sub>, then rank-correlate each recorded forecast with observed breadth. The page computes these Spearman correlations live from the embedded records; at 0 it reproduces the run's 0.768 and 0.770.</p>
    <div class="controls" style="display:block">
      <label for="w-p" class="clabel">Keep concepts with OPEN<sub>home</sub> at or above percentile: <output id="w-pv" for="w-p">0</output></label>
      <input type="range" id="w-p" min="0" max="80" step="5" value="0" aria-describedby="w-read">
      <p class="statusline" id="w-read"></p>
    </div>
    <div class="legend" aria-hidden="true"><span><i class="sw-line b"></i>Baseline forecast (B5)</span><span><i class="sw-line"></i>B5 + OPEN<sub>home</sub></span></div>
    <div class="chart" id="chart-sweep"></div>
    <p class="takeaway" id="take-sweep" aria-live="polite"></p>
  </div>
</div>
</section>

<!-- ============ 5. WHERE IT FAILS ============ -->
<section class="block" id="fails" aria-labelledby="h-fails">
<div class="wrap">
  <h2 id="h-fails">Where it fails</h2>
  <div class="view" id="v-checks">
    <p class="q">Which pre-registered checks on the retained-frontier result held, and which did not?</p>
    <p class="small" style="margin:0">All on held-out data. The frozen rule needed every criterion; one failed, so the verdict is PARTIAL.</p>
    <div class="controls">
      <fieldset><legend>Show</legend><div class="seg" role="radiogroup" aria-label="Which checks">
        <label><input type="radio" name="x-show" value="all" checked><span>All checks</span></label>
        <label><input type="radio" name="x-show" value="fail"><span>Only failures</span></label>
      </div></fieldset>
    </div>
    <div class="legend" aria-hidden="true"><span><i class="sw-sq" style="border-radius:50%"></i>Held</span><span><i class="sw-fail"></i>Failed or reversed</span></div>
    <div class="chart" id="chart-checks"></div>
    <p class="takeaway" id="take-checks" aria-live="polite"></p>
  </div>

  <div class="view">
    <p class="q">Where does OPEN make a single forecast worse?</p>
    <p>The item browser above can isolate these cases. <button type="button" class="btn" id="go-fail" style="min-height:40px;padding:6px 12px">Show the cases where OPEN moved the forecast away</button></p>
    <p class="count" id="fail-count"></p>
  </div>

  <div class="prose">
    <h3>What the paper does not show</h3>
    <ul class="limits">
      <li><strong>No forecasting gain.</strong> OPEN<sub>home</sub> adds +0.002 [−0.003, +0.008] Spearman over B5 on the fresh cohort.</li>
      <li><strong>Marginal on the home-only build.</strong> On the 2015–17 cohort it passes rung R2 (+0.091, 95% CI [+0.013, +0.171], Holm p = 0.048), but its DerSimonian–Laird interval over groups includes zero (+0.083 [−0.007, +0.173]).</li>
      <li><strong>Static, not temporal.</strong> A within-concept year-permutation null absorbs the churn: excess NOVCHURN gives +0.008 against +0.116 raw. The temporal-excess measure has split-half reliability of about 0.01–0.05, so temporal turnover is untested rather than refuted.</li>
      <li><strong>Not a within-concept mechanism.</strong> The closure test is null on DEV and opposite-signed on held-out fields (−0.079 [−0.146, −0.013]).</li>
      <li><strong>Coupling.</strong> About half of the OPEN<sub>all</sub> signal is mechanical: early off-home papers enter both the ego network and the breadth outcome.</li>
      <li><strong>Noise and domains.</strong> Split-half reliability of OPEN<sub>home</sub> is 0.49. Life &amp; Environment shows the weakest signal (PSP +0.042).</li>
      <li><strong>Retained frontier.</strong> The volume-matched contrast is null, the dose response is not monotone, and d<sub>0</sub> reverses under minimum-conditional-probability proximity. Persistence and volume stay confounded, and the effect is specific to the PMI backbone.</li>
      <li><strong>Not causal, and survivor-selected.</strong> Openness could reflect a concept's generality or its community. The legacy vocabulary is survivor-selected; the vocabulary-free Frame N has 636 concepts and a partial verdict.</li>
    </ul>
  </div>
</div>
</section>
</main>
