<script>
(function(){
"use strict";
const $ = (s, r=document) => r.querySelector(s);
const $$ = (s, r=document) => Array.from(r.querySelectorAll(s));
const load = id => JSON.parse(document.getElementById(id).textContent);
const EV = load("data-evidence"), SCR = load("data-screen"), CO = load("data-cohort"),
      PR = load("data-pairs"), EN = load("data-entry"), CH = load("data-cheng");
const NS = "http://www.w3.org/2000/svg";
const MINUS = "−";

/* ---------- formatting ---------- */
function rnd(x, d){ const m = Math.pow(10, d); return Math.round((x + (x >= 0 ? 1e-12 : -1e-12)) * m) / m; }
function f(x, d=3){ if (x === null || x === undefined || !isFinite(x)) return "n/a"; let s = rnd(x, d).toFixed(d); if (s.startsWith("-")) { s = (/^-0\.0*$/.test(s) ? "" : MINUS) + s.slice(1); } return s; }
function fs(x, d=3){ const s = f(x, d); return (x >= 0 || s.indexOf(MINUS) < 0) && !s.startsWith(MINUS) ? "+" + s : s; }
function ci(c, d=3, signed=false){ const g = signed ? fs : f; return "[" + g(c[0], d) + ", " + g(c[1], d) + "]"; }
function int(n){ return Number(n).toLocaleString("en-US"); }
function esc(s){ return String(s).replace(/[&<>"]/g, c => ({"&":"&amp;","<":"&lt;",">":"&gt;",'"':"&quot;"}[c])); }

/* ---------- svg helpers ---------- */
function svgEl(tag, attrs, parent){ const e = document.createElementNS(NS, tag); if (attrs) for (const k in attrs) e.setAttribute(k, attrs[k]); if (parent) parent.appendChild(e); return e; }
function newSvg(container, h){ container.innerHTML = ""; const w = Math.max(280, container.clientWidth || 600); const s = svgEl("svg", {width: w, height: h, viewBox: `0 0 ${w} ${h}`}); container.appendChild(s); return {svg: s, w}; }
function textWidth(svg, strings, cls){ const g = svgEl("g", {}, svg); let m = 0; for (const s of strings){ const t = svgEl("text", {class: cls}, g); t.textContent = s; m = Math.max(m, t.getComputedTextLength ? t.getComputedTextLength() : s.length * 7); } svg.removeChild(g); return m; }
function niceTicks(lo, hi, n){ const span = hi - lo; const raw = span / Math.max(1, n); const p = Math.pow(10, Math.floor(Math.log10(raw))); const m = raw / p; const step = (m < 1.5 ? 1 : m < 3 ? 2 : m < 7 ? 5 : 10) * p; const out = []; for (let v = Math.ceil(lo / step - 1e-9) * step; v <= hi + 1e-9; v += step) out.push(Math.abs(v) < step / 1e6 ? 0 : v); return {ticks: out, step}; }
function tickFmt(v, step){ const d = Math.max(0, -Math.floor(Math.log10(step) + 1e-9)); return f(v, d); }

/* ---------- chart tooltip ---------- */
const tip = $("#charttip"); let tipOwner = null;
function showTip(target, html){ tip.innerHTML = html; tip.classList.add("on"); tipOwner = target; const r = target.getBoundingClientRect(); const tw = Math.min(300, window.innerWidth - 20); tip.style.maxWidth = tw + "px"; const th = tip.offsetHeight; let x = r.left + r.width / 2 - tip.offsetWidth / 2; x = Math.max(8, Math.min(window.innerWidth - tip.offsetWidth - 8, x)); let y = r.top - th - 10; if (y < 50) y = r.bottom + 10; tip.style.left = x + "px"; tip.style.top = y + "px"; }
function hideTip(){ tip.classList.remove("on"); tipOwner = null; }
function bindMark(g, html, label){ g.setAttribute("class", "mark"); g.setAttribute("tabindex", "0"); g.setAttribute("role", "img"); g.setAttribute("aria-label", label); const h = typeof html === "function" ? html : () => html; g.addEventListener("mouseenter", () => showTip(g, h())); g.addEventListener("mouseleave", hideTip); g.addEventListener("focus", () => showTip(g, h())); g.addEventListener("blur", hideTip); g.addEventListener("click", ev => { ev.stopPropagation(); showTip(g, h()); }); }
document.addEventListener("keydown", e => { if (e.key === "Escape") { hideTip(); closeTerms(); } });
document.addEventListener("click", e => { if (tipOwner && !tipOwner.contains(e.target)) hideTip(); });
window.addEventListener("scroll", hideTip, {passive: true});

/* ---------- generic horizontal interval chart ---------- */
/* rows: {label, est, ci|null, kind:'main'|'dim'|'fail'|'pool', band:number|null, tip, aria, sep} */
function intervalChart(container, rows, opt){
  const rowH = opt.rowH || 34, top = 8, bottom = 50;
  const h = top + rows.length * rowH + (rows.some(r => r.sep) ? 10 : 0) + bottom;
  const {svg, w} = newSvg(container, h);
  const labW = textWidth(svg, rows.map(r => r.label), "rowlab");
  const left = Math.ceil(labW) + 16, right = 18;
  let lo = opt.min !== undefined ? opt.min : Infinity, hi = opt.max !== undefined ? opt.max : -Infinity;
  for (const r of rows){ const vals = [r.est].concat(r.ci || []); if (r.band) vals.push(-r.band, r.band); for (const v of vals) if (isFinite(v)) { lo = Math.min(lo, v); hi = Math.max(hi, v); } }
  lo = Math.min(lo, 0); hi = Math.max(hi, 0); const pad = (hi - lo) * 0.06; lo -= pad; hi += pad;
  const pw = w - left - right; const X = v => left + (v - lo) / (hi - lo) * pw;
  const nt = Math.max(2, Math.floor(pw / 70)); const {ticks, step} = niceTicks(lo, hi, nt);
  const plotBottom = h - bottom;
  const grid = svgEl("g", {class: "grid"}, svg), tk = svgEl("g", {class: "tick"}, svg);
  for (const t of ticks){ if (t < lo || t > hi) continue; svgEl("line", {x1: X(t), x2: X(t), y1: top, y2: plotBottom}, grid); const tx = svgEl("text", {x: X(t), y: plotBottom + 17, "text-anchor": "middle"}, tk); tx.textContent = tickFmt(t, step); }
  svgEl("line", {x1: left, x2: w - right, y1: plotBottom, y2: plotBottom, stroke: "#9aa3ad"}, svg);
  svgEl("line", {x1: X(0), x2: X(0), y1: top, y2: plotBottom, stroke: "#6a7380", "stroke-dasharray": "4 3"}, svg);
  if (opt.ref !== undefined && opt.ref !== null){ svgEl("line", {x1: X(opt.ref), x2: X(opt.ref), y1: top, y2: plotBottom, stroke: "#1b1f24", "stroke-dasharray": "1 3", "stroke-width": 1.4}, svg); }
  const at = svgEl("text", {x: left + pw / 2, y: h - 8, "text-anchor": "middle", class: "axis-title"}, svg); at.textContent = opt.xTitle;
  let y = top;
  rows.forEach(r => {
    if (r.sep){ svgEl("line", {x1: 0, x2: w - right, y1: y + 5, y2: y + 5, stroke: "#c9ced4"}, svg); y += 10; }
    const cy = y + rowH / 2;
    const lab = svgEl("text", {x: left - 12, y: cy + 4.5, "text-anchor": "end", class: "rowlab" + (r.kind === "dim" ? " dim" : "")}, svg); lab.textContent = r.label;
    if (r.kind === "pool") lab.setAttribute("font-weight", "700");
    const g = svgEl("g", {}, svg);
    if (r.band){ svgEl("rect", {x: X(-r.band), width: X(r.band) - X(-r.band), y: cy - 8, height: 16, fill: "#eef0f2", stroke: "#d4d8dd"}, g); }
    const col = r.kind === "dim" ? "var(--base)" : r.kind === "fail" ? "var(--fail)" : r.kind === "pool" ? "var(--ink)" : "var(--accent)";
    if (r.kind === "pool" && r.ci){ const x0 = X(r.ci[0]), x1 = X(r.ci[1]), xm = X(r.est); svgEl("path", {d: `M${x0},${cy} L${xm},${cy - 8} L${x1},${cy} L${xm},${cy + 8} Z`, fill: "var(--ink)"}, g); }
    else {
      if (r.ci){ svgEl("line", {x1: X(r.ci[0]), x2: X(r.ci[1]), y1: cy, y2: cy, stroke: col, "stroke-width": 2.4}, g); for (const v of r.ci) svgEl("line", {x1: X(v), x2: X(v), y1: cy - 5, y2: cy + 5, stroke: col, "stroke-width": 2}, g); }
      if (opt.shape === "circle" || r.kind === "fail") svgEl("circle", {cx: X(r.est), cy, r: 6, fill: col}, g);
      else svgEl("rect", {x: X(r.est) - 6, y: cy - 6, width: 12, height: 12, fill: col}, g);
    }
    svgEl("rect", {class: "hit", x: left - 4, y: y + 1, width: pw + 8, height: rowH - 2, rx: 4}, g);
    bindMark(g, r.tip, r.aria);
    y += rowH;
  });
  return svg;
}

/* ---------- vertical/horizontal bars from zero ---------- */
function barChart(container, rows, opt){
  const rowH = opt.rowH || 36, top = 8, bottom = 50;
  const h = top + rows.length * rowH + bottom; const {svg, w} = newSvg(container, h);
  const labW = textWidth(svg, rows.map(r => r.label), "rowlab"); const left = Math.ceil(labW) + 16, right = 18;
  let lo = 0, hi = 0; for (const r of rows){ for (const v of [r.v].concat(r.ci || [])) { lo = Math.min(lo, v); hi = Math.max(hi, v); } }
  if (opt.min !== undefined) lo = Math.min(lo, opt.min); if (opt.max !== undefined) hi = Math.max(hi, opt.max);
  const pad = (hi - lo) * 0.06; lo -= pad; hi += pad;
  const pw = w - left - right, X = v => left + (v - lo) / (hi - lo) * pw, plotBottom = h - bottom;
  const {ticks, step} = niceTicks(lo, hi, Math.max(2, Math.floor(pw / 70)));
  const grid = svgEl("g", {class: "grid"}, svg), tk = svgEl("g", {class: "tick"}, svg);
  for (const t of ticks){ if (t < lo || t > hi) continue; svgEl("line", {x1: X(t), x2: X(t), y1: top, y2: plotBottom}, grid); const tx = svgEl("text", {x: X(t), y: plotBottom + 17, "text-anchor": "middle"}, tk); tx.textContent = tickFmt(t, step); }
  svgEl("line", {x1: left, x2: w - right, y1: plotBottom, y2: plotBottom, stroke: "#9aa3ad"}, svg);
  const at = svgEl("text", {x: left + pw / 2, y: h - 8, "text-anchor": "middle", class: "axis-title"}, svg); at.textContent = opt.xTitle;
  rows.forEach((r, i) => {
    const y = top + i * rowH, cy = y + rowH / 2;
    const lab = svgEl("text", {x: left - 12, y: cy + 4.5, "text-anchor": "end", class: "rowlab"}, svg); lab.textContent = r.label;
    const g = svgEl("g", {}, svg);
    const col = r.color || (r.v < 0 ? "var(--fail)" : "var(--accent)");
    svgEl("rect", {x: Math.min(X(0), X(r.v)), y: cy - 9, width: Math.max(1.5, Math.abs(X(r.v) - X(0))), height: 18, fill: col, opacity: r.muted ? 0.45 : 0.9}, g);
    if (r.ci){ svgEl("line", {x1: X(r.ci[0]), x2: X(r.ci[1]), y1: cy, y2: cy, stroke: "#1b1f24", "stroke-width": 1.6}, g); for (const v of r.ci) svgEl("line", {x1: X(v), x2: X(v), y1: cy - 5, y2: cy + 5, stroke: "#1b1f24", "stroke-width": 1.6}, g); }
    svgEl("rect", {class: "hit", x: left - 4, y: y + 1, width: pw + 8, height: rowH - 2, rx: 4}, g);
    bindMark(g, r.tip, r.aria);
  });
  svgEl("line", {x1: X(0), x2: X(0), y1: top, y2: plotBottom, stroke: "#1b1f24", "stroke-width": 1.2}, svg);
}

/* ---------- term tooltips ---------- */
const GLOSS = {
  OPEN: ["OPEN index", "The mean of six signed z-scored ego-network components from the early window (t<sub>0</sub> to t<sub>0</sub>+2): new edge rate, number of Leiden communities reached, participation coefficient and neighbourhood novelty residual count positive; ego density and edge persistence count negative. It measures a concept's early tendency to acquire novel, community-spanning co-occurrence partners."],
  OPENhome: ["OPEN<sub>home</sub>", "The OPEN index built on the home-field co-occurrence graph only. OPEN<sub>all</sub> uses the corpus-wide graph and OPEN<sub>sizematch</sub> subsamples corpus-wide papers to home counts."],
  NOVCHURN: ["NOVCHURN", "The mean of z(NOV<sub>res</sub>) and −z(edge persistence), a two-component novelty/churn measure used in the mechanism analyses."],
  B5: ["Five-feature baseline (B5)", "Log early volume, publication growth, non-home share, Shannon entropy and field reach, all computed over t<sub>0</sub> to t<sub>0</sub>+2."],
  PSP: ["Partial Spearman priority (PSP)", "The Pearson correlation of rank-transformed indicator and outcome residuals, both residualised on the baseline covariates and control rungs. Inference uses 2,000 concept-level bootstrap resamples with refit."],
  O2r: ["Rarefied field breadth (O<sub>2r</sub>)", "The expected number of distinct venue fields among a fixed-size random draw of m = 50 papers from a concept's publications in years t<sub>0</sub>+6 to t<sub>0</sub>+8, computed by exact hypergeometric rarefaction. Rarefaction separates size-adjusted breadth from sheer volume."],
  onset: ["Onset year (t<sub>0</sub>)", "The first year a concept reaches 20 grounded publications."],
  home: ["Home field", "The field(s) holding at least 40% of the first 30 grounded papers."],
  DEV: ["Development set (DEV)", "Concepts with Computer Science, Engineering, Biochemistry/Genetics/Medicine homes and onsets 2003–2009, on which indicators were selected and the specification frozen."],
  nonsel: ["Non-selection body", "A body of concepts not used to choose the index: the four held-out home groups (Physical Sciences, Life & Environment, Social Sciences, Math & Decision), the 2010–14 onset cohort and the 2015–17 onset cohort."],
  DL: ["DerSimonian–Laird pool", "The random-effects estimator used to pool estimates across field groups, reported with I<sup>2</sup> heterogeneity."],
  I2: ["I<sup>2</sup>", "The share of variation across pooled bodies that reflects real heterogeneity rather than sampling error. 0 means the bodies agree within noise."],
  rung: ["Control rung", "A step in the control ladder. R0 controls for B5 (plus onset year); R2 adds contact reach, concept type, a generic-concept flag and concept level; R3 adds the pre-onset footprint. Higher rungs are more demanding."],
  placebo: ["Shuffled-feature 95th percentile", "The absolute partial Spearman that a randomly permuted copy of the index reaches in 95% of 200 permutations in that body. An estimate inside this band is indistinguishable from noise for that body alone."],
  Holm: ["Holm correction", "A step-down correction for multiple comparisons across the pre-declared family of tests."],
  ego: ["Ego network", "The concept's positive-PMI neighbour topics in the early window; edges are links between those topics in the topic backbone."],
  leiden: ["Leiden community", "A cluster of topics found by Leiden community detection on the topic co-occurrence backbone."],
  NOVres: ["Neighbourhood novelty residual (NOV<sub>res</sub>)", "The novelty of a concept's co-occurrence partners after residualising on degree."],
  persist: ["Edge persistence", "The fraction of the concept's neighbours retained across windows."],
  newedge: ["New edge rate", "The fraction of a concept's co-occurrence neighbours that are new."],
  particip: ["Participation coefficient", "The share of a concept's ties that cross community boundaries."],
  density: ["Ego density", "The density of the concept's local co-occurrence subgraph."],
  retaining: ["Retaining field", "A field is retaining a concept when it has published at least two grounded papers on the concept in each of the two most recent years."],
  d0: ["Retained-frontier coefficient (d<sub>0</sub>)", "Log-odds of entering a field per SD of relatedness to the off-home fields that currently retain the concept, from the conditional-logit entry model."],
  condlogit: ["Conditional logit", "A Breslow partial-likelihood model on concept-year risk sets, stratified by concept-year, that compares the field a concept actually enters with the fields it could have entered that year."],
  PMI: ["PMI backbone", "Relatedness between fields measured by positive pointwise mutual information on the frozen 1998–2002 field-level backbone."],
  volmatch: ["Volume-matched contrast", "Compares entry rates of retained versus entered-but-not-retained fields in the same volume cell. Pre-registered criterion 5 needs its CI above zero."],
  mincp: ["Minimum-conditional-probability proximity", "The standard proximity of Hidalgo et al. (2007), used as an alternative to the PMI backbone."],
  consistency: ["Ideational consistency", "Cheng et al.'s (2023) measure, rebuilt on OpenAlex topic co-usage: the cosine similarity of a concept's topic co-usage from one year to the next. It has Spearman +0.77 with edge persistence."]
};
const termTips = [];
function closeTerms(except){ termTips.forEach(t => { if (t !== except) t.hidden = true; }); }
function placeTip(btn, t){ const r = btn.getBoundingClientRect(); const tw = Math.min(330, window.innerWidth - 20); t.style.maxWidth = tw + "px"; t.hidden = false; let x = Math.max(8, Math.min(window.innerWidth - t.offsetWidth - 8, r.left)); let y = r.bottom + 6; if (y + t.offsetHeight > window.innerHeight - 8) y = Math.max(8, r.top - t.offsetHeight - 6); t.style.left = x + "px"; t.style.top = y + "px"; }
function initTerms(root){
  $$(".term", root).forEach((b, i) => {
    if (b.dataset.bound) return; b.dataset.bound = "1";
    const g = GLOSS[b.dataset.term]; if (!g) return;
    const t = document.createElement("span"); t.className = "tip"; t.id = "tt-" + b.dataset.term + "-" + termTips.length; t.setAttribute("role", "tooltip"); t.hidden = true;
    t.innerHTML = "<strong>" + g[0] + "</strong>" + g[1]; document.body.appendChild(t); termTips.push(t);
    b.setAttribute("aria-describedby", t.id);
    const open = () => { closeTerms(t); placeTip(b, t); };
    b.addEventListener("mouseenter", open); b.addEventListener("focus", open);
    b.addEventListener("click", e => { e.stopPropagation(); open(); });
    b.addEventListener("mouseleave", () => { if (document.activeElement !== b) t.hidden = true; });
    b.addEventListener("blur", () => { t.hidden = true; });
  });
}
document.addEventListener("click", () => closeTerms());
window.addEventListener("scroll", () => closeTerms(), {passive: true});

/* ================= 1. FINDING ================= */
const BODY = {B2_PHYS: "Physical Sciences", B2_LIFEENV: "Life & Environment", B2_SOC: "Social Sciences", B2_MATHDEC: "Math & Decision", B3_EXP5_COHORT_2010_14: "2010–14 cohort", B4_COHORT_2015_17: "2015–17 cohort", B1_DEV: "DEV (selection)"};
const BODY_ORDER = ["B2_PHYS", "B2_LIFEENV", "B2_SOC", "B2_MATHDEC", "B3_EXP5_COHORT_2010_14", "B4_COHORT_2015_17"];
function getRadio(name){ return ($(`input[name="${name}"]:checked`) || {}).value; }
function drawFinding(){
  const feat = getRadio("f-feat"), rung = getRadio("f-rung"), dev = $("#f-dev").checked;
  const pool = EV.pools[feat + "|" + rung];
  const rows = [];
  BODY_ORDER.forEach(b => {
    const r = EV.rows.find(x => x.body === b && x.feature === feat); if (!r) return;
    const inPool = pool.bodies.includes(b); const v = r[rung];
    const status = inPool ? (r.status === "confirmatory" ? "never used in any earlier step" : "outcomes read in earlier analyses") : "selection body for this index (not pooled)";
    rows.push({label: BODY[b], est: v.psp, ci: v.ci, kind: inPool ? "main" : "dim", band: r.placebo_p95,
      aria: `${BODY[b]}: ${fs(v.psp)} ${ci(v.ci, 3, true)}, n ${v.n}`,
      tip: `<b>${BODY[b]}</b> (onsets ${r.onsets})<br>PSP at ${rung}: <b>${fs(v.psp)}</b> ${ci(v.ci, 3, true)}<br>n = ${int(v.n)} concepts analysed of ${int(r.n_body)}<br>Shuffled-feature 95th pct: ±${f(r.placebo_p95)}<br>${status}`});
  });
  rows.push({label: "Pool, " + pool.k + " bodies", est: pool.est, ci: pool.ci, kind: "pool", sep: true,
    aria: `Pooled ${fs(pool.est)} ${ci(pool.ci, 3, true)}`,
    tip: `<b>DerSimonian–Laird pool</b> over ${pool.k} non-selection bodies<br><b>${fs(pool.est)}</b> ${ci(pool.ci, 3, true)}<br>I² = ${f(pool.I2, 2)}; ${pool.sign} positive`});
  if (dev){ const r = EV.rows.find(x => x.body === "B1_DEV" && x.feature === feat); const v = r[rung];
    rows.push({label: "DEV (selection)", est: v.psp, ci: v.ci, kind: "dim", band: r.placebo_p95, sep: true, aria: `DEV: ${fs(v.psp)} ${ci(v.ci, 3, true)}`,
      tip: `<b>DEV selection body</b> (onsets 2003–09)<br>PSP at ${rung}: <b>${fs(v.psp)}</b> ${ci(v.ci, 3, true)}<br>n = ${int(v.n)}<br>The index was chosen here; not pooled. ${f(pool.shrink, 2)}× the pool.`}); }
  intervalChart($("#chart-finding"), rows, {xTitle: "Partial Spearman with rarefied breadth O2r (m = 50), net of controls", ref: pool.est});
  const main = rows.filter(r => r.kind === "main");
  const above = main.filter(r => r.ci[0] > 0).length, pos = main.filter(r => r.est > 0).length;
  const name = feat === "OPEN_home" ? "OPEN home" : "NOVCHURN home";
  $("#take-finding").textContent = `At ${rung}, ${name} is positive in ${pos} of ${main.length} pooled bodies and its pooled estimate is ${fs(pool.est)} ${ci(pool.ci, 3, true)} with I² = ${f(pool.I2, 2)}; ${above} of ${main.length} bodies have a CI above zero on their own, and the selection body sits ${f(pool.shrink, 2)}× higher than the pool.`;
  $("#finding-rungnote").textContent = feat === "NOVCHURN_home" ? "NOVCHURN was chosen on the 2015–17 cohort, so that body is greyed and left out of its pool (k = 5)." : "R2 is the primary rung: B5 plus onset year, contact reach, concept type, a generic-concept flag and concept level.";
  if (feat === "OPEN_home" && rung === "R2"){ $("#big-num").textContent = fs(pool.est); $("#big-ci").innerHTML = `95% CI ${ci(pool.ci, 3, true)}, I<sup>2</sup> = ${f(pool.I2, 0)}, ${pool.sign.replace("/", " of ")} bodies positive. Pooled partial Spearman of OPEN<sub>home</sub> with rarefied breadth over six non-selection bodies, at the primary rung R2.`; }
}
$$('input[name="f-feat"], input[name="f-rung"], #f-dev').forEach(i => i.addEventListener("change", drawFinding));

/* ================= 2. STEPPER ================= */
const P1 = PR.pairs[0], GPU = P1.members.HIGH_OPEN, VAWT = P1.members.LOW_OPEN;
const ZC = PR.z_constants, COMPS = PR.components;
const CNAME = {new_edge_rate: "New edge rate", n_comm_W3: "Communities reached", participation: "Participation coefficient", NOV_res: "Novelty residual NOV_res", ego_density_W3: "Ego density", edge_persistence: "Edge persistence"};
const CTERM = {new_edge_rate: "newedge", n_comm_W3: "leiden", participation: "particip", NOV_res: "NOVres", ego_density_W3: "density", edge_persistence: "persist"};
function openScore(comp, build, use){ const z = []; COMPS.forEach(([k, s]) => { if (!use || use.includes(k)) { const v = comp[build][k]; if (v !== null && isFinite(v)) z.push(s * (v - ZC[build][k].mean) / ZC[build][k].sd); } }); return z.length >= 4 ? z.reduce((a, b) => a + b, 0) / z.length : null; }
function twoCol(rows){ return `<table><thead><tr><th scope="col"></th><th scope="col" class="num">GPU</th><th scope="col" class="num">VAWT</th></tr></thead><tbody>${rows.map(r => `<tr><th scope="row">${r[0]}</th><td class="num">${r[1]}</td><td class="num">${r[2]}</td></tr>`).join("")}</tbody></table>`; }
const es = (m, k) => m.ego_snapshot_stats[(m === GPU ? "HIGH_OPEN_" : "LOW_OPEN_") + k];
const homePool = EV.pools["OPEN_home|R2"];
const STAGES = [
  {short: "Ground", title: "1. Ground the concept in the literature",
   in: () => `<p>Titles of 129.4M base works (1995–2022) from the OpenAlex snapshot, and 56,643 legacy OpenAlex concepts.</p>`,
   do: () => `<p>Aho–Corasick title matching plus an LLM precision gate keeps concepts whose matches are at least 0.80 precise. The <button type="button" class="term" data-term="onset">onset year</button> and <button type="button" class="term" data-term="home">home field</button> are then fixed.</p>`,
   out: () => twoCol([["Onset t<sub>0</sub>", GPU.t0, VAWT.t0], ["Home field (OpenAlex id)", "Engineering (" + GPU.home + ")", "Engineering (" + VAWT.home + ")"], ["Reporting group", GPU.group, VAWT.group]]),
   why: "A shared clock and a home field make “early” and “off-home” mean the same thing for every concept."},
  {short: "B5 window", title: "2. Measure early popularity: the baseline",
   in: () => `<p>The concept's grounded papers in its first three years, t<sub>0</sub> to t<sub>0</sub>+2.</p>`,
   do: () => `<p>Compute the five <button type="button" class="term" data-term="B5">B5</button> features. Any network signal must add information beyond these.</p>`,
   out: () => twoCol([["Log early volume", f(GPU.B5.logvol, 3), f(VAWT.B5.logvol, 3)], ["Growth", f(GPU.B5.growth_c, 3), f(VAWT.B5.growth_c, 3)], ["Non-home share", f(GPU.B5.offhome_share, 3), f(VAWT.B5.offhome_share, 3)], ["Field entropy", f(GPU.B5.entropy, 3), f(VAWT.B5.entropy, 3)], ["Field reach", f(GPU.B5.reach, 0), f(VAWT.B5.reach, 0)]]),
   why: "The pair was matched on early volume and growth, so those two cannot separate them. GPU already reaches more fields early, which is why the real test scores OPEN net of all of B5."},
  {short: "Ego network", title: "3. Build the early ego network",
   in: () => `<p>The topics that co-occur with the concept in its first three years, and the topic backbone that links topics to each other.</p>`,
   do: () => `<p>Keep the positive-PMI neighbour topics as the <button type="button" class="term" data-term="ego">ego network</button>, link them through the backbone, and label each with its <button type="button" class="term" data-term="leiden">Leiden community</button>. The home build uses home-field papers only.</p>`,
   out: () => twoCol([["Topics (all papers)", es(GPU, "W3_all").n_nodes, es(VAWT, "W3_all").n_nodes], ["Links", es(GPU, "W3_all").n_edges, es(VAWT, "W3_all").n_edges], ["Communities", es(GPU, "W3_all").n_communities, es(VAWT, "W3_all").n_communities], ["Density", f(es(GPU, "W3_all").density, 2), f(es(VAWT, "W3_all").density, 2)], ["Topics, home papers", es(GPU, "W3_home").n_nodes, es(VAWT, "W3_home").n_nodes], ["Communities, home", es(GPU, "W3_home").n_communities, es(VAWT, "W3_home").n_communities]]) + `<p class="small" style="margin-top:8px">GPU's top neighbours: ${GPU.top_W3_neighbours.slice(0, 4).map(n => esc(n[0])).join("; ")}. VAWT's: ${VAWT.top_W3_neighbours.slice(0, 4).map(n => esc(n[0])).join("; ")}.</p>`,
   why: "GPU's early partners already sit in 8 communities; VAWT's sit in one. This is the difference OPEN is built to measure.", fig: true},
  {short: "OPEN", title: "4. Turn six components into one index",
   in: () => twoCol(COMPS.map(([k]) => [CNAME[k] + " (home)", f(GPU.components.home[k], 3), f(VAWT.components.home[k], 3)])),
   do: () => `<p>z-score each component with constants frozen over all 12,499 frame concepts, flip the sign of density and persistence, and average. The page recomputes this now from the recorded components.</p>`,
   out: () => { const gh = openScore(GPU.components, "home"), vh = openScore(VAWT.components, "home"), ga = openScore(GPU.components, "all"), va = openScore(VAWT.components, "all");
     return twoCol([["OPEN<sub>home</sub>, computed here", f(gh, 3), f(vh, 3)], ["OPEN<sub>home</sub>, recorded", f(GPU.OPEN.home, 3), f(VAWT.OPEN.home, 3)], ["OPEN<sub>all</sub>, computed here", f(ga, 3), f(va, 3)], ["OPEN<sub>all</sub>, recorded", f(GPU.OPEN.all, 3), f(VAWT.OPEN.all, 3)]]) + `<p class="small" style="margin-top:8px">Largest difference between computed and recorded: ${Math.max(Math.abs(gh - GPU.OPEN.home), Math.abs(vh - VAWT.OPEN.home), Math.abs(ga - GPU.OPEN.all), Math.abs(va - VAWT.OPEN.all)).toExponential(1)}.</p>`; },
   why: "A single signed average keeps the index interpretable: each unit is one standard deviation of openness across the frame. The Try it section runs the same computation for all 14 case-study concepts."},
  {short: "Breadth", title: "5. Observe breadth six to eight years later",
   in: () => `<p>The concept's papers in years t<sub>0</sub>+6 to t<sub>0</sub>+8, and its entries into off-home venue fields each year.</p>`,
   do: () => `<p>Draw 50 papers at random (exactly, by hypergeometric rarefaction) and count the expected number of distinct venue fields: <button type="button" class="term" data-term="O2r">rarefied breadth</button>.</p>`,
   out: () => twoCol([["Rarefied breadth O<sub>2r</sub> (m = 50)", f(GPU.outcomes.O2r_m50, 2), f(VAWT.outcomes.O2r_m50, 2)], ["O<sub>2r</sub> size-residual", fs(GPU.outcomes.O2r_resid, 2), fs(VAWT.outcomes.O2r_resid, 2)], ["Off-home fields entered by t<sub>0</sub>+2", f(GPU.decomposition.E2, 0), f(VAWT.decomposition.E2, 0)], ["Ever entered by t<sub>0</sub>+8", f(GPU.decomposition.EH, 0), f(VAWT.decomposition.EH, 0)], ["Retained at t<sub>0</sub>+8", f(GPU.decomposition.Bn, 0), f(VAWT.decomposition.Bn, 0)]]),
   why: "Rarefaction removes sheer volume from breadth. Breadth was not used to pick the pair; it is shown only after selection, and in 7 of 7 case pairs the more open concept is broader. That is an illustration, not evidence."},
  {short: "Pool", title: "6. Test across thousands of concepts and pool",
   in: () => `<p>OPEN<sub>home</sub>, breadth and the control covariates for every concept in each body of data.</p>`,
   do: () => `<p>Within each body, compute the <button type="button" class="term" data-term="PSP">partial Spearman</button> of OPEN<sub>home</sub> with breadth after the controls of rung R2, with 2,000 concept bootstraps. Pool the six non-selection bodies with <button type="button" class="term" data-term="DL">DerSimonian–Laird</button>.</p>`,
   out: () => `<p style="font-size:1.6rem;font-weight:700;color:var(--accent);margin:0">${fs(homePool.est)}</p><p>${ci(homePool.ci, 3, true)}, I<sup>2</sup> = ${f(homePool.I2, 0)}, ${homePool.sign} positive; DEV selection body ${fs(homePool.dev)} (${f(homePool.shrink, 2)}× the pool).</p>`,
   why: "One pair shows the mechanism; only the pooled test across bodies that did not choose the index says whether the pattern is general."}
];
let cur = 0;
function drawPipeline(){
  const c = $("#pipeline"); const narrow = (c.clientWidth || 600) < 600; const cols = narrow ? 3 : 6, rowsN = narrow ? 2 : 1;
  const {svg, w} = newSvg(c, rowsN * 64 + 8); const gap = 14, bw = (w - gap * (cols - 1)) / cols;
  STAGES.forEach((s, i) => { const col = i % cols, row = Math.floor(i / cols); const x = col * (bw + gap), y = 4 + row * 64;
    const on = i === cur, done = i < cur;
    const g = svgEl("g", {style: "cursor:pointer"}, svg);
    svgEl("rect", {x, y, width: bw, height: 50, rx: 8, fill: on ? "var(--accent)" : done ? "var(--accent-soft)" : "#fff", stroke: on || done ? "var(--accent)" : "#b9c0c8", "stroke-width": 1.5}, g);
    const t = svgEl("text", {x: x + bw / 2, y: y + 30, "text-anchor": "middle", "font-size": 13, "font-weight": 600, style: `fill:${on ? "#fff" : "var(--ink)"}`}, g); t.textContent = (i + 1) + ". " + s.short;
    if (i < STAGES.length - 1 && col < cols - 1){ svgEl("path", {d: `M${x + bw + 2},${y + 25} l${gap - 5},0 m-5,-4 l5,4 l-5,4`, stroke: "#8a939e", fill: "none", "stroke-width": 1.5}, svg); }
    g.addEventListener("click", () => go(i)); });
}
function drawStage(){
  const s = STAGES[cur];
  $("#step-title").textContent = s.title; $("#step-in").innerHTML = s.in(); $("#step-do").innerHTML = s.do(); $("#step-out").innerHTML = s.out(); $("#step-why").textContent = "Why: " + s.why;
  $("#step-fig").hidden = !s.fig;
  $$("#step-markers button").forEach((b, i) => { if (i === cur) b.setAttribute("aria-current", "step"); else b.removeAttribute("aria-current"); });
  $("#step-prev").disabled = cur === 0; $("#step-next").disabled = cur === STAGES.length - 1;
  $("#step-live").textContent = `Stage ${cur + 1} of ${STAGES.length}: ${s.title.replace(/^\d+\.\s*/, "")}`;
  drawPipeline(); initTerms($("#stepper"));
}
function go(i){ cur = Math.max(0, Math.min(STAGES.length - 1, i)); drawStage(); }
STAGES.forEach((s, i) => { const li = document.createElement("li"); const b = document.createElement("button"); b.type = "button"; b.textContent = (i + 1) + ". " + s.short; b.setAttribute("aria-label", `Stage ${i + 1}: ${s.title.replace(/^\d+\.\s*/, "")}`); b.addEventListener("click", () => go(i)); li.appendChild(b); $("#step-markers").appendChild(li); });
$("#step-prev").addEventListener("click", () => go(cur - 1)); $("#step-next").addEventListener("click", () => go(cur + 1));
$("#stepper").addEventListener("keydown", e => { if (e.target.matches("input,select,textarea")) return; if (e.key === "ArrowRight") { go(cur + 1); e.preventDefault(); } else if (e.key === "ArrowLeft") { go(cur - 1); e.preventDefault(); } });

/* ================= 3a. SCREEN ================= */
const INDNAME = {M0_density_end: "M0_density_end", D_vol_end: "D_vol_end", CONTACT_REACH: "CONTACT_REACH", n_comm_W3: "n_comm (W3)", NOV: "NOV_res", RETENTION_RATIO_early: "RETENTION_RATIO", ego_density_W3: "ego_density (W3)", RS: "Rao–Stirling", G_btw: "G_btw", log_offhome_volume: "log offhome vol."};
const FAM = {FR: "retained frontier", A: "co-occurrence ego network", G: "gateway / diversity", F: "disciplinary", E: "popularity", S: "co-author"};
const UNITNAME = {PHYS: "Physical Sciences", LIFEENV: "Life & Environment", SOC: "Social Sciences", MATHDEC: "Math & Decision", COH_DEVHOME: "2010–14 cohort, DEV homes", COH_OTHER: "2010–14 cohort, other homes"};
function drawScreen(){
  const unit = $("#s-unit").value, sort = $("#s-sort").value, conf = $("#s-conf").checked;
  let rows = SCR.filter(r => !conf || r.conf).map(r => { const est = unit === "pooled" ? r.pooled : r.unit[unit], c = unit === "pooled" ? r.ci : r.unit_ci[unit];
    return {r, est, c}; });
  if (sort === "est") rows.sort((a, b) => b.est - a.est); else if (sort === "abs") rows.sort((a, b) => Math.abs(b.est) - Math.abs(a.est)); else rows.sort((a, b) => a.r.fam.localeCompare(b.r.fam) || b.est - a.est);
  const ch = rows.map(({r, est, c}) => ({label: INDNAME[r.ind] || r.ind, est, ci: c, kind: r.conf ? "main" : "dim",
    aria: `${INDNAME[r.ind]}: ${fs(est)} ${ci(c, 3, true)}${r.conf ? ", confirmed" : ", not confirmed"}`,
    tip: `<b>${INDNAME[r.ind]}</b> (family ${r.fam}: ${FAM[r.fam]})<br>${unit === "pooled" ? "Pooled PSP" : UNITNAME[unit] + " PSP"}: <b>${fs(est)}</b> ${ci(c, 3, true)}` + (unit === "pooled" ? `<br>I² = ${f(r.I2, 2)}; sign agreement ${r.sign}/${r.n_units}` : `<br>n = ${int(r.unit_n[unit])}`) + `<br>${r.conf ? "Confirmed (Holm p < 0.05, CI excludes 0)" : "Not confirmed"}`}));
  intervalChart($("#chart-screen"), ch, {xTitle: unit === "pooled" ? "Pooled partial Spearman with O2r (m = 50), net of B5" : "Partial Spearman with O2r (m = 50), net of B5, " + UNITNAME[unit]});
  const nConf = SCR.filter(r => r.conf).length;
  const excl = rows.filter(x => x.c[0] > 0 || x.c[1] < 0).length;
  const top = rows.slice().sort((a, b) => Math.abs(b.est) - Math.abs(a.est))[0];
  $("#take-screen").textContent = (unit === "pooled" ? `${nConf} of 10 frozen indicators are confirmed on held-out data; ` : `In ${UNITNAME[unit]}, ${excl} of ${rows.length} shown indicators have a CI that excludes zero; `) + `the largest shown is ${INDNAME[top.r.ind]} at ${fs(top.est)}. The two negative confirmed indicators, RETENTION_RATIO and ego density, say that concepts which keep their early fields or sit in dense neighbourhoods spread less broadly.`;
}
["#s-unit", "#s-sort", "#s-conf"].forEach(s => $(s).addEventListener("change", drawScreen));

/* ================= 3b. ITEM BROWSER ================= */
const ITEMS = CO.items.map((d, i) => Object.assign({i, has: d.y !== null && d.pb !== null && d.po !== null}, d));
ITEMS.forEach(d => { if (d.has) { d.eb = Math.abs(d.pb - d.y); d.eo = Math.abs(d.po - d.y); d.gain = d.eb - d.eo; d.worse = d.eo > d.eb; d.res = d.y - d.pb; } });
const GROUPS = [...new Set(ITEMS.map(d => d.g))].sort(), TYPES = [...new Set(ITEMS.map(d => d.ty))].sort();
GROUPS.forEach(g => $("#b-group").insertAdjacentHTML("beforeend", `<option value="${esc(g)}">${esc(g)}</option>`));
TYPES.forEach(t => $("#b-type").insertAdjacentHTML("beforeend", `<option value="${esc(t)}">${esc(t)}</option>`));
let selItem = null, listLimit = 60;
function filtered(){
  const q = $("#b-q").value.trim().toLowerCase(), g = $("#b-group").value, t = $("#b-type").value, obs = $("#b-obs").checked, fail = $("#b-fail").checked;
  let r = ITEMS.filter(d => (!q || d.c.toLowerCase().includes(q)) && (!g || d.g === g) && (!t || d.ty === t) && (!obs || d.has) && (!fail || (d.has && d.worse)));
  const s = $("#b-sort").value;
  const key = {open: d => -(d.oh === null ? -1e9 : d.oh), gain: d => -(d.has ? d.gain : -1e9), hurt: d => (d.has ? d.gain : 1e9), y: d => -(d.y === null ? -1e9 : d.y)}[s];
  if (s === "name") r.sort((a, b) => a.c.localeCompare(b.c)); else r.sort((a, b) => key(a) - key(b));
  return r;
}
function drawBrowser(keepSel){
  const r = filtered();
  if (!keepSel || !selItem || !r.includes(selItem)) selItem = r[0] || null;
  const withY = r.filter(d => d.has), worse = withY.filter(d => d.worse).length;
  $("#b-count").textContent = `${int(r.length)} concepts match; ${int(withY.length)} have both forecasts and an observed outcome.`;
  const ul = $("#b-list"); ul.innerHTML = "";
  r.slice(0, listLimit).forEach(d => { const li = document.createElement("li"); const b = document.createElement("button"); b.type = "button"; b.setAttribute("aria-pressed", d === selItem ? "true" : "false");
    b.innerHTML = `<span>${esc(d.c)}</span><span class="meta">OPEN ${d.oh === null ? "n/a" : fs(d.oh, 2)}${d.has ? (d.worse ? " · worse" : " · better") : ""}</span>`;
    b.addEventListener("click", () => { selItem = d; drawBrowser(true); }); li.appendChild(b); ul.appendChild(li); });
  $("#b-more").innerHTML = r.length > listLimit ? `Showing ${listLimit} of ${int(r.length)}. <button type="button" class="btn" id="b-morebtn" style="min-height:40px;padding:4px 12px">Show 60 more</button>` : "";
  if ($("#b-morebtn")) $("#b-morebtn").addEventListener("click", () => { listLimit += 60; drawBrowser(true); });
  drawDetail(); drawScatter(r);
  if (withY.length){ const med = withY.map(d => d.gain).sort((a, b) => a - b)[Math.floor(withY.length / 2)];
    $("#take-browser").textContent = `Of the ${int(withY.length)} concepts shown with an observed outcome, adding OPEN home brought the forecast closer for ${int(withY.length - worse)} and moved it away for ${int(worse)}; the median change in absolute error is ${f(med, 3)} fields, so the typical concept's forecast barely moves.`; }
  else $("#take-browser").textContent = "No concept in this selection has an observed outcome, so neither forecast can be scored.";
  $("#fail-count").textContent = `Across all ${int(ITEMS.filter(d => d.has).length)} scored cohort concepts, OPEN moved the forecast away from observed breadth for ${int(ITEMS.filter(d => d.has && d.worse).length)}.`;
}
function drawDetail(){
  const d = selItem, el = $("#b-detail");
  if (!d){ el.innerHTML = "<p>No concept matches these filters.</p>"; return; }
  const yv = d.y === null ? "n/a" : f(d.y, 2);
  el.innerHTML = `<h3 style="margin-bottom:2px">${esc(d.c)}</h3><p class="small" style="margin:0 0 6px">OpenAlex ${esc(d.id)} · onset ${d.t0} · home group ${esc(d.g)} · type ${esc(d.ty)}</p>
  <div class="cmp"><div class="base"><div class="v">${d.pb === null ? "n/a" : f(d.pb, 2)}</div><div class="l">Baseline forecast<br>(B5 only)</div></div>
  <div class="meth"><div class="v">${d.po === null ? "n/a" : f(d.po, 2)}</div><div class="l">Forecast with<br>B5 + OPEN<sub>home</sub></div></div>
  <div><div class="v">${yv}</div><div class="l">Observed breadth<br>O<sub>2r</sub>, m = 50</div></div></div>
  ${d.has ? `<p class="statusline">Absolute error: baseline ${f(d.eb, 2)}, with OPEN ${f(d.eo, 2)}. <span class="pill ${d.worse ? "bad" : "ok"}">${d.worse ? "OPEN moved it away" : "OPEN moved it closer"}</span></p>` : `<p class="statusline">${d.y === null ? "No observed outcome: too few papers in t<sub>0</sub>+6 to t<sub>0</sub>+8 for m = 50." : "OPEN<sub>home</sub> is undefined (fewer than 10 early home papers), so only the baseline forecast exists."}</p>`}
  <h4 style="margin-top:10px">Input: early window t<sub>0</sub> to t<sub>0</sub>+2</h4>
  <div class="tscroll"><table><tbody>
  <tr><th scope="row">Log early volume</th><td class="num">${f(d.lv, 3)}</td><th scope="row">OPEN<sub>home</sub></th><td class="num">${d.oh === null ? "n/a" : fs(d.oh, 3)}</td></tr>
  <tr><th scope="row">Growth</th><td class="num">${f(d.gr, 3)}</td><th scope="row">OPEN<sub>all</sub></th><td class="num">${d.oa === null ? "n/a" : fs(d.oa, 3)}</td></tr>
  <tr><th scope="row">Non-home share</th><td class="num">${f(d.sh, 3)}</td><th scope="row">OPEN<sub>size</sub></th><td class="num">${d.os === null ? "n/a" : fs(d.os, 3)}</td></tr>
  <tr><th scope="row">Field entropy</th><td class="num">${f(d.en, 3)}</td><th scope="row">Early home papers</th><td class="num">${d.nh}</td></tr>
  <tr><th scope="row">Field reach</th><td class="num">${f(d.re, 0)}</td><td></td><td></td></tr></tbody></table></div>`;
}
let scatterPts = [];
function drawScatter(r){
  const pts = r.filter(d => d.has && d.oh !== null);
  const c = $("#chart-scatter"); const H = 300; const {svg, w} = newSvg(c, H);
  const top = 10, bottom = 48;
  let xlo = Math.min(...ITEMS.filter(d => d.has && d.oh !== null).map(d => d.oh)), xhi = Math.max(...ITEMS.filter(d => d.has && d.oh !== null).map(d => d.oh));
  let ylo = Math.min(...ITEMS.filter(d => d.has).map(d => d.res)), yhi = Math.max(...ITEMS.filter(d => d.has).map(d => d.res));
  const px = (xhi - xlo) * 0.04, py = (yhi - ylo) * 0.05; xlo -= px; xhi += px; ylo -= py; yhi += py;
  const yt = niceTicks(ylo, yhi, 5); const ylabW = textWidth(svg, yt.ticks.map(t => tickFmt(t, yt.step)), "tick");
  const left = Math.ceil(ylabW) + 8 + 22, right = 12, pw = w - left - right, ph = H - top - bottom;
  const X = v => left + (v - xlo) / (xhi - xlo) * pw, Y = v => top + (yhi - v) / (yhi - ylo) * ph;
  const grid = svgEl("g", {class: "grid"}, svg), tk = svgEl("g", {class: "tick"}, svg);

content</a>\n<header class=\"top\">\n  <div class=\"wrap\">\n    <p class=\"small\" style=\"margin:0 0 .4rem\">Interactive companion to the paper</p>\n    <h1>Early co-occurrence network openness predicts cross-disciplinary concept breadth: evidence from 12,499 scientific concepts</h1>\n    <p class=\"authors\">AI Inventor</p>\n    <div class=\"links\">\n      <a class=\"btn primary\" href=\"https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/gh/ai-inventor-papers/ai-invention-8795ea-concepts-spread-once-adopters-make-them@fork/run_kLBLH5WmvR9Y/paper.pdf\">Read the paper (PDF)</a>\n      <a class=\"btn\" href=\"https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/gh/ai-inventor-papers/ai-invention-8795ea-concepts-spread-once-adopters-make-them@fork/run_kLBLH5WmvR9Y/report.pdf\">Read the full research report</a>\n      <a class=\"btn\" href=\"https://github.com/ai-inventor-papers/ai-invention-8795ea-concepts-spread-once-adopters-make-them/tree/fork/run_kLBLH5WmvR9Y\">Code repository</a>\n    </div>\n  </div>\n</header>\n<nav class=\"sections\" aria-label=\"Page sections\">\n  <ul>\n    <li><a href=\"#finding\">The finding</a></li>\n    <li><a href=\"#how\">How it works</a></li>\n    <li><a href=\"#evidence\">Explore the evidence</a></li>\n    <li><a href=\"#try\">Try it</a></li>\n    <li><a href=\"#fails\">Where it fails</a></li>\n    <li><a href=\"#notes\">Links, data, glossary</a></li>\n  </ul>\n</nav>\n<main id=\"main\">\n\n<!-- ============ 1. FINDING ============ -->\n<section class=\"block\" id=\"finding\" aria-labelledby=\"h-finding\">\n<div class=\"wrap\">\n  <h2 id=\"h-finding\">The finding</h2>\n  <div class=\"grid2\">\n    <div class=\"prose\">\n      <p class=\"q\">Which early signals in a concept's topic network tell us whether it will later spread across many fields?</p>\n      <p>Popularity already explains a lot. A five-feature <button type=\"button\" class=\"term\" data-term=\"B5\">popularity baseline</button> reaches Spearman 0.65–0.86 with later breadth, so any network signal has to add something beyond it. The paper screens 53 early indicators and composes the survivors into the <button type=\"button\" class=\"term\" data-term=\"OPEN\">OPEN index</button>: a concept's early tendency to acquire novel, community-spanning co-occurrence partners.</p>\n      <p>Measured on the concept's home field only, and net of the baseline, OPEN has the same sign in every body of data that was not used to choose it:</p>\n      <div class=\"bignum\" id=\"big-num\" aria-describedby=\"big-ci\"></div>\n      <div class=\"bignum-ci\" id=\"big-ci\"></div>\n      <p>The association is small, and the pool is descriptive: all non-selection bodies except the 2015–17 cohort had outcomes read in earlier analyses. It adds almost nothing to a forecast. What it shows is a consistent direction: concepts whose early partners span more topic communities reach more fields later.</p>\n    </div>\n    <div class=\"view\" style=\"margin-top:0\">\n      <p class=\"q\">Does the association hold in every body of data?</p>\n      <p class=\"small\" style=\"margin:0\">Each row is one body of concepts. The value is the <button type=\"button\" class=\"term\" data-term=\"PSP\">partial Spearman</button> of the index with <button type=\"button\" class=\"term\" data-term=\"O2r\">rarefied breadth</button>, after removing what the baseline explains.</p>\n      <div class=\"controls\">\n        <fieldset><legend>Index</legend><div class=\"seg\" role=\"radiogroup\" aria-label=\"Index\">\n          <label><input type=\"radio\" name=\"f-feat\" value=\"OPEN_home\" checked><span>OPEN<sub>home</sub></span></label>\n          <label><input type=\"radio\" name=\"f-feat\" value=\"NOVCHURN_home\"><span>NOVCHURN<sub>home</sub></span></label>\n        </div></fieldset>\n        <fieldset><legend>Control rung</legend><div class=\"seg\" role=\"radiogroup\" aria-label=\"Control rung\">\n          <label><input type=\"radio\" name=\"f-rung\" value=\"R0\"><span>R0</span></label>\n          <label><input type=\"radio\" name=\"f-rung\" value=\"R2\" checked><span>R2</span></label>\n          <label><input type=\"radio\" name=\"f-rung\" value=\"R3\"><span>R3</span></label>\n        </div></fieldset>\n        <label class=\"check\"><input type=\"checkbox\" id=\"f-dev\" checked> Show the selection body</label>\n      </div>\n      <div class=\"legend\" aria-hidden=\"true\">\n        <span><i class=\"sw-sq\"></i>Non-selection body, 95% CI</span>\n        <span><i class=\"sw-dev\"></i>Selection body (not pooled)</span>\n        <span><i class=\"sw-band\"></i>Shuffled-feature 95th percentile</span>\n        <span><i class=\"sw-dia\"></i>DerSimonian–Laird pool</span>\n      </div>\n      <div class=\"chart\" id=\"chart-finding\"></div>\n      <p class=\"small\" id=\"finding-rungnote\"></p>\n      <p class=\"takeaway\" id=\"take-finding\" aria-live=\"polite\"></p>\n    </div>\n  </div>\n</div>\n</section>\n\n<!-- ============ 2. HOW IT WORKS ============ -->\n<section class=\"block\" id=\"how\" aria-labelledby=\"h-how\">\n<div class=\"wrap\">\n  <h2 id=\"h-how\">How it works</h2>\n  <div class=\"prose\">\n    <p class=\"q\">What does the method do to one concept, from raw papers to a pooled estimate?</p>\n    <p>Follow the graphics processing unit (GPU) through the six stages, with its matched partner, the vertical-axis wind turbine (VAWT), beside it. Both have an Engineering home and were matched on early volume and growth before their outcomes were looked at. Every value below is the one the run recorded for them.</p>\n  </div>\n  <div class=\"view\" id=\"stepper\" tabindex=\"-1\" aria-roledescription=\"stepper\">\n    <div class=\"chart\" id=\"pipeline\" aria-hidden=\"true\"></div>\n    <ol class=\"steps\" id=\"step-markers\" aria-label=\"Stages\"></ol>\n    <div class=\"stepnav\">\n      <button type=\"button\" id=\"step-prev\">&larr; Previous</button>\n      <button type=\"button\" id=\"step-next\">Next &rarr;</button>\n      <span class=\"small\">Left and right arrow keys also move between stages.</span>\n    </div>\n    <div id=\"step-live\" class=\"sr\" aria-live=\"polite\"></div>\n    <h3 id=\"step-title\"></h3>\n    <div class=\"stage\">\n      <div class=\"box\"><h4>What goes in</h4><div id=\"step-in\"></div></div>\n      <div class=\"box\"><h4>What is done</h4><div id=\"step-do\"></div></div>\n      <div class=\"box\"><h4>What comes out</h4><div id=\"step-out\"></div></div>\n    </div>\n    <p class=\"why\" id=\"step-why\"></p>\n    <figure id=\"step-fig\" hidden>\n      <img src=\"figures/fig_case_study_v0.png\" alt=\"Three panels. Left: step lines of off-home fields entered and retained by year since onset; GPU climbs to 11 entered and 8 retained by year 8, VAWT to 6 and 4. Middle: GPU's early ego network, 34 topic nodes in 8 coloured communities, loosely connected. Right: VAWT's ego network, 12 nodes all in one Engineering community, tightly connected.\" loading=\"lazy\" width=\"1300\" height=\"560\">\n      <figcaption>Illustrative matched case-study pair from Experiment 12 (case pair 1 of 7): graphics processing unit (GPU; onset t<sub>0</sub>=2008, high early-neighbourhood openness OPEN) versus vertical-axis wind turbine (VAWT; t<sub>0</sub>=2009, low OPEN). Both have an Engineering home field and are matched on early volume and growth. (a) Number of off-home venue fields each concept has ever entered (solid line, filled markers) and currently retains (dashed line, open markers) in each year from t<sub>0</sub> to t<sub>0</sub>+8. (b, c) Topic co-occurrence ego networks over the first three years (t<sub>0</sub> to t<sub>0</sub>+2, all papers); colour gives the topic's Leiden community. GPU's neighbourhood has 34 topics in 8 communities (density 0.30). VAWT's has 12 topics in a single Engineering community (density 0.70). The pair illustrates the openness–breadth association and is not evidence for it.</figcaption>\n    </figure>\n  </div>\n  <figure>\n    <img src=\"figures/fig_overview_v0.jpg\" alt=\"Study design flow: OpenAlex snapshot (476M works) to concept identification (56,643 legacy concepts, 12,499 grounded), to a panel split (DEV 4,771; held-out 3,372; cohort 4,356; fresh cohort 1,443), to 53 indicators in six families, feeding RQ1 screen and validate (7 confirmed, OPEN pooled +0.069) and, separately, RQ2 conditional logit (11,841 concepts, d0 = 0.322, verdict PARTIAL).\" loading=\"lazy\" width=\"2000\" height=\"858\">\n    <figcaption>Overview of the study design, read left to right. The OpenAlex snapshot (476M works, 129.4M base works 1995–2022) is title-matched against 56,643 legacy concepts, and Aho–Corasick matching plus an LLM precision gate keeps 12,499 grounded concepts. The panel split assigns these to a development set (DEV 4,771), four held-out domain groups (3,372) and a 2010–2014 onset cohort (4,356). A fresh 2015–2017 cohort (1,443) comes from a separate scan. For each concept, 53 early indicators in six families are computed in the t<sub>0</sub> to t<sub>0</sub>+2 window, screened on DEV and validated on held-out groups (RQ1). Separately, a conditional-logit entry model is fitted on an independent frame of 11,841 concepts (RQ2).</figcaption>\n  </figure>\n</div>\n</section>\n\n<!-- ============ 3. EVIDENCE ============ -->\n<section class=\"block\" id=\"evidence\" aria-labelledby=\"h-evidence\">\n<div class=\"wrap\">\n  <h2 id=\"h-evidence\">Explore the evidence</h2>\n\n  <div class=\"view\" id=\"v-screen\">\n    <p class=\"q\">Which of the frozen early indicators survive testing on held-out fields?</p>\n    <p class=\"small\" style=\"margin:0\">The 10 indicators ranked highest on DEV, each tested once on four held-out field groups and two cohort splits. Confirmation needs Holm-corrected p &lt; 0.05 and a pooled 95% CI that excludes zero.</p>\n    <div class=\"controls\">\n      <label><span class=\"clabel\">Show estimate for</span>\n        <select id=\"s-unit\">\n          <option value=\"pooled\">DerSimonian–Laird pool (6 units)</option>\n          <option value=\"PHYS\">Physical Sciences</option>\n          <option value=\"LIFEENV\">Life &amp; Environment</option>\n          <option value=\"SOC\">Social Sciences</option>\n          <option value=\"MATHDEC\">Math &amp; Decision</option>\n          <option value=\"COH_DEVHOME\">2010–14 cohort, DEV homes</option>\n          <option value=\"COH_OTHER\">2010–14 cohort, other homes</option>\n        </select></label>\n      <label><span class=\"clabel\">Order</span>\n        <select id=\"s-sort\"><option value=\"est\">By estimate</option><option value=\"abs\">By size, ignoring sign</option><option value=\"fam\">By family</option></select></label>\n      <label class=\"check\"><input type=\"checkbox\" id=\"s-conf\"> Confirmed only</label>\n    </div>\n    <div class=\"legend\" aria-hidden=\"true\"><span><i class=\"sw-sq\"></i>Confirmed</span><span><i class=\"sw-dev\"></i>Not confirmed</span></div>\n    <div class=\"chart\" id=\"chart-screen\"></div>\n    <p class=\"takeaway\" id=\"take-screen\" aria-live=\"polite\"></p>\n  </div>\n\n  <div class=\"view\" id=\"v-browser\">\n    <p class=\"q\">What does OPEN change for one concept's forecast?</p>\n    <p class=\"small\" style=\"margin:0\">All 1,443 concepts of the fresh 2015–2017 cohort, the one body never used in any earlier step. For each, the run recorded two frozen forecasts of breadth fitted on the earlier frame: the baseline (B5 only) and B5 plus OPEN<sub>home</sub>. The chart plots every concept with an observed outcome: OPEN<sub>home</sub> against how far the observed breadth sits above or below the baseline forecast. Click a point or a list row.</p>\n    <div class=\"controls\">\n      <label><span class=\"clabel\">Search</span><input type=\"search\" id=\"b-q\" placeholder=\"Concept name\" aria-label=\"Search concepts by name\"></label>\n      <label><span class=\"clabel\">Home group</span><select id=\"b-group\"><option value=\"\">All groups</option></select></label>\n      <label><span class=\"clabel\">Concept type</span><select id=\"b-type\"><option value=\"\">All types</option></select></label>\n      <label><span class=\"clabel\">Sort list by</span><select id=\"b-sort\">\n        <option value=\"open\">OPEN<sub>home</sub>, high to low</option>\n        <option value=\"gain\">OPEN helped most</option>\n        <option value=\"hurt\">OPEN hurt most</option>\n        <option value=\"y\">Observed breadth, high to low</option>\n        <option value=\"name\">Name</option></select></label>\n      <label class=\"check\"><input type=\"checkbox\" id=\"b-obs\" checked> Only concepts with an observed outcome</label>\n      <label class=\"check\"><input type=\"checkbox\" id=\"b-fail\"> Only cases where OPEN moved the forecast away</label>\n    </div>\n    <p class=\"count\" id=\"b-count\" aria-live=\"polite\"></p>\n    <div class=\"legend\" aria-hidden=\"true\"><span><i class=\"sw-dev\" style=\"border-radius:50%\"></i>Concept</span><span><i class=\"sw-fail\"></i>OPEN moved forecast away from observed</span><span><i class=\"sw-sq\" style=\"border-radius:50%\"></i>Selected</span></div>\n    <div class=\"chart\" id=\"chart-scatter\" tabindex=\"0\" role=\"img\" aria-label=\"Scatter of OPEN home against observed breadth minus baseline forecast. Use left and right arrow keys to move the selection through points.\"></div>\n    <div class=\"browser\" style=\"margin-top:14px\">\n      <div><ul class=\"list\" id=\"b-list\" aria-label=\"Concepts\"></ul><p class=\"small\" id=\"b-more\"></p></div>\n      <div class=\"detail\" id=\"b-detail\" aria-live=\"polite\"></div>\n    </div>\n    <p class=\"takeaway\" id=\"take-browser\" aria-live=\"polite\"></p>\n  </div>\n\n  <div class=\"view\" id=\"v-entry\">\n    <p class=\"q\">Does a concept next enter fields related to the fields that currently keep it?</p>\n    <p class=\"small\" style=\"margin:0\">A separate question on an independent frame of 11,841 concepts. The <button type=\"button\" class=\"term\" data-term=\"condlogit\">conditional logit</button> asks which field a concept enters next; <button type=\"button\" class=\"term\" data-term=\"d0\">d<sub>0</sub></button> is the extra log-odds per SD of relatedness to the <button type=\"button\" class=\"term\" data-term=\"retaining\">retaining fields</button>, after home relatedness, field size, entered density, own gateway centrality, RCA density and volume density.</p>\n    <div class=\"controls\">\n      <label class=\"check\"><input type=\"checkbox\" id=\"e-dev\" checked> Show DEV (selection data)</label>\n      <label class=\"check\"><input type=\"checkbox\" id=\"e-pool\" checked> Show held-out pool</label>\n    </div>\n    <div class=\"legend\" aria-hidden=\"true\"><span><i class=\"sw-sq\" style=\"border-radius:50%\"></i>Held-out unit, 95% concept-bootstrap CI</span><span><i class=\"sw-dev\" style=\"border-radius:50%\"></i>DEV</span><span><i class=\"sw-dia\"></i>DerSimonian–Laird pool, 4 held-out groups</span></div>\n    <div class=\"chart\" id=\"chart-entry\"></div>\n    <p class=\"takeaway\" id=\"take-entry\" aria-live=\"polite\"></p>\n  </div>\n\n  <div class=\"view\" id=\"v-cheng\">\n    <p class=\"q\">If an open neighbourhood goes with breadth, does a stable one go with growth?</p>\n    <p class=\"small\" style=\"margin:0\">The paper rebuilt Cheng et al.'s <button type=\"button\" class=\"term\" data-term=\"consistency\">ideational consistency</button> for 12,311 concepts. Bars start at zero; whiskers are 95% concept-bootstrap CIs.</p>\n    <div class=\"controls\">\n      <fieldset><legend>View</legend><div class=\"seg\" role=\"radiogroup\" aria-label=\"Consistency view\">\n        <label><input type=\"radio\" name=\"c-view\" value=\"out\" checked><span>By outcome</span></label>\n        <label><input type=\"radio\" name=\"c-view\" value=\"grp\"><span>Reach, by field group</span></label>\n      </div></fieldset>\n    </div>\n    <div class=\"chart\" id=\"chart-cheng\"></div>\n    <p class=\"takeaway\" id=\"take-cheng\" aria-live=\"polite\"></p>\n  </div>\n</div>\n</section>\n\n<!-- ============ 4. TRY IT ============ -->\n<section class=\"block\" id=\"try\" aria-labelledby=\"h-try\">\n<div class=\"wrap\">\n  <h2 id=\"h-try\">Try it</h2>\n  <div class=\"view\" id=\"v-calc\">\n    <p class=\"q\">Can I compute OPEN myself and get the recorded value?</p>\n    <p class=\"small\" style=\"margin:0\">The index is simple enough to run here exactly. Each of the six components is z-scored with the constants frozen over all 12,499 frame concepts, signed (density and persistence count against openness), and averaged when at least 4 of 6 are present. Pick one of the 14 case-study concepts and a build; untick components to see how much each carries.</p>\n    <div class=\"controls\">\n      <label><span class=\"clabel\">Concept</span><select id=\"k-concept\"></select></label>\n      <fieldset><legend>Build</legend><div class=\"seg\" role=\"radiogroup\" aria-label=\"Build\">\n        <label><input type=\"radio\" name=\"k-build\" value=\"home\" checked><span>Home only</span></label>\n        <label><input type=\"radio\" name=\"k-build\" value=\"all\"><span>All papers</span></label>\n        <label><input type=\"radio\" name=\"k-build\" value=\"size\"><span>Size-matched</span></label>\n      </div></fieldset>\n    </div>\n    <fieldset><legend>Components used</legend><div class=\"controls\" id=\"k-comps\" style=\"margin-top:0\"></div></fieldset>\n    <div class=\"grid2\" style=\"grid-template-columns:minmax(0,6fr) minmax(0,5fr)\">\n      <div class=\"tscroll\"><table id=\"k-table\"><caption class=\"sr\">OPEN computation for the selected concept</caption><thead><tr><th scope=\"col\">Component</th><th scope=\"col\" class=\"num\">Recorded</th><th scope=\"col\" class=\"num\">Mean</th><th scope=\"col\" class=\"num\">SD</th><th scope=\"col\" class=\"num\">Signed z</th></tr></thead><tbody></tbody></table></div>\n      <div><div class=\"chart\" id=\"chart-calc\"></div></div>\n    </div>\n    <p class=\"statusline\" id=\"k-status\" aria-live=\"polite\"></p>\n    <p class=\"takeaway\" id=\"take-calc\" aria-live=\"polite\"></p>\n  </div>\n\n  <div class=\"view\" id=\"v-sweep\">\n    <p class=\"q\">Does OPEN improve the forecast for the most open concepts?</p>\n    <p class=\"small\" style=\"margin:0\">Over the 573 cohort concepts that have both forecasts and an observed outcome, keep only those at or above a percentile of OPEN<sub>home</sub>, then rank-correlate each recorded forecast with observed breadth. The page computes these Spearman correlations live from the embedded records; at 0 it reproduces the run's 0.768 and 0.770.</p>\n    <div class=\"controls\" style=\"display:block\">\n      <label for=\"w-p\" class=\"clabel\">Keep concepts with OPEN<sub>home</sub> at or above percentile: <output id=\"w-pv\" for=\"w-p\">0</output></label>\n      <input type=\"range\" id=\"w-p\" min=\"0\" max=\"80\" step=\"5\" value=\"0\" aria-describedby=\"w-read\">\n      <p class=\"statusline\" id=\"w-read\"></p>\n    </div>\n    <div class=\"legend\" aria-hidden=\"true\"><span><i class=\"sw-line b\"></i>Baseline forecast (B5)</span><span><i class=\"sw-line\"></i>B5 + OPEN<sub>home</sub></span></div>\n    <div class=\"chart\" id=\"chart-sweep\"></div>\n    <p class=\"takeaway\" id=\"take-sweep\" aria-live=\"polite\"></p>\n  </div>\n</div>\n</section>\n\n<!-- ============ 5. WHERE IT FAILS ============ -->\n<section class=\"block\" id=\"fails\" aria-labelledby=\"h-fails\">\n<div class=\"wrap\">\n  <h2 id=\"h-fails\">Where it fails</h2>\n  <div class=\"view\" id=\"v-checks\">\n    <p class=\"q\">Which pre-registered checks on the retained-frontier result held, and which did not?</p>\n    <p class=\"small\" style=\"margin:0\">All on held-out data. The frozen rule needed every criterion; one failed, so the verdict is PARTIAL.</p>\n    <div class=\"controls\">\n      <fieldset><legend>Show</legend><div class=\"seg\" role=\"radiogroup\" aria-label=\"Which checks\">\n        <label><input type=\"radio\" name=\"x-show\" value=\"all\" checked><span>All checks</span></label>\n        <label><input type=\"radio\" name=\"x-show\" value=\"fail\"><span>Only failures</span></label>\n      </div></fieldset>\n    </div>\n    <div class=\"legend\" aria-hidden=\"true\"><span><i class=\"sw-sq\" style=\"border-radius:50%\"></i>Held</span><span><i class=\"sw-fail\"></i>Failed or reversed</span></div>\n    <div class=\"chart\" id=\"chart-checks\"></div>\n    <p class=\"takeaway\" id=\"take-checks\" aria-live=\"polite\"></p>\n  </div>\n\n  <div class=\"view\">\n    <p class=\"q\">Where does OPEN make a single forecast worse?</p>\n    <p>The item browser above can isolate these cases. <button type=\"button\" class=\"btn\" id=\"go-fail\" style=\"min-height:40px;padding:6px 12px\">Show the cases where OPEN moved the forecast away</button></p>\n    <p class=\"count\" id=\"fail-count\"></p>\n  </div>\n\n  <div class=\"prose\">\n    <h3>What the paper does not show</h3>\n    <ul class=\"limits\">\n      <li><strong>No forecasting gain.</strong> OPEN<sub>home</sub> adds +0.002 [−0.003, +0.008] Spearman over B5 on the fresh cohort.</li>\n      <li><strong>Marginal on the home-only build.</strong> On the 2015–17 cohort it passes rung R2 (+0.091, 95% CI [+0.013, +0.171], Holm p = 0.048), but its DerSimonian–Laird interval over groups includes zero (+0.083 [−0.007, +0.173]).</li>\n      <li><strong>Static, not temporal.</strong> A within-concept year-permutation null absorbs the churn: excess NOVCHURN gives +0.008 against +0.116 raw. The temporal-excess measure has split-half reliability of about 0.01–0.05, so temporal turnover is untested rather than refuted.</li>\n      <li><strong>Not a within-concept mechanism.</strong> The closure test is null on DEV and opposite-signed on held-out fields (−0.079 [−0.146, −0.013]).</li>\n      <li><strong>Coupling.</strong> About half of the OPEN<sub>all</sub> signal is mechanical: early off-home papers enter both the ego network and the breadth outcome.</li>\n      <li><strong>Noise and domains.</strong> Split-half reliability of OPEN<sub>home</sub> is 0.49. Life &amp; Environment shows the weakest signal (PSP +0.042).</li>\n      <li><strong>Retained frontier.</strong> The volume-matched contrast is null, the dose response is not monotone, and d<sub>0</sub> reverses under minimum-conditional-probability proximity. Persistence and volume stay confounded, and the effect is specific to the PMI backbone.</li>\n      <li><strong>Not causal, and survivor-selected.</strong> Openness could reflect a concept's generality or its community. The legacy vocabulary is survivor-selected; the vocabulary-free Frame N has 636 concepts and a partial verdict.</li>\n    </ul>\n  </div>\n</div>\n</section>\n</main>\n\n<!-- ============ FOOTER ============ -->\n<footer id=\"notes\" aria-labelledby=\"h-notes\">\n<div class=\"wrap\">\n  <h2 id=\"h-notes\" style=\"margin-top:0\">Links</h2>\n  <div class=\"links\">\n    <a class=\"btn primary\" href=\"https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/gh/ai-inventor-papers/ai-invention-8795ea-concepts-spread-once-adopters-make-them@fork/run_kLBLH5WmvR9Y/paper.pdf\">Read the paper (PDF)</a>\n    <a class=\"btn\" href=\"https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/gh/ai-inventor-papers/ai-invention-8795ea-concepts-spread-once-adopters-make-them@fork/run_kLBLH5WmvR9Y/report.pdf\">Read the full research report</a>\n    <a class=\"btn\" href=\"https://github.com/ai-inventor-papers/ai-invention-8795ea-concepts-spread-once-adopters-make-them/tree/fork/run_kLBLH5WmvR9Y\">Code repository</a>\n  </div>\n  <h2>Where each view's data comes from</h2>\n  <p class=\"small\">Every chart, count and table on this page is built in the browser from JSON embedded in this file, extracted by script from the run's output files. Nothing is typed in by hand.</p>\n  <ul id=\"provenance\"></ul>\n  <h2>Glossary</h2>\n  <dl class=\"gloss cols2\" id=\"glossary\"></dl>\n  <h2>Cite</h2>\n  <p class=\"small\">AI Inventor. <em>Early co-occurrence network openness predicts cross-disciplinary concept breadth: evidence from 12,499 scientific concepts.</em></p>\n</div>\n</footer>\n<div id=\"charttip\" role=\"status\" aria-live=\"polite\"></div>\n\n<!--DATA-->\n\n<script>\n(function(){\n\"use strict\";\nconst $ = (s, r=document) => r.querySelector(s);\nconst $$ = (s, r=document) => Array.from(r.querySelectorAll(s));\nconst load = id => JSON.parse(document.getElementById(id).textContent);\nconst EV = load(\"data-evidence\"), SCR = load(\"data-screen\"), CO = load(\"data-cohort\"),\n      PR = load(\"data-pairs\"), EN = load(\"data-entry\"), CH = load(\"data-cheng\");\nconst NS = \"http://www.w3.org/2000/svg\";\nconst MINUS = \"−\";\n\n/* ---------- formatting ---------- */\nfunction rnd(x, d){ const m = Math.pow(10, d);   const H2 = hNow + 16; svg.setAttribute("height", H2); svg.setAttribute("viewBox", `0 0 ${w} ${H2}`);
  const cxx = Math.max(bd / 2 + 2, Math.min(w - bd / 2 - 2, cx));
  [words.slice(0, best).join(" "), words.slice(best).join(" ")].forEach((line, i) => { const t = svgEl("text", {x: cxx, y: hNow - 8 + i * 16, "text-anchor": "middle", class: "axis-title"}, svg); t.textContent = line; }); }

No centrality or volume-only indicator survives. <a href=\"https://github.com/ai-inventor-papers/ai-invention-8795ea-concepts-spread-once-adopters-make-them/tree/fork/run_kLBLH5WmvR9Y/round-3/experiment-8\">Code</a></p>\n483:    <p class=\"result-body\">Conditional logit on the independent held-out frame (11,841 concepts, 6,978 entry events, 6,076 informative strata). Positive in three of three evaluable held-out groups: Physical Sciences +0.148, Life &amp; Environment +0.401, Social Sciences +0.297. Mathematics &amp; Decision Sciences (n = 165, excluded as underpowered before the freeze) is null: 0.065 [&minus;0.110, 0.234]. The DerSimonian-Laird pooled estimate over four held-out groups is 0.243 [0.118, 0.368] with I<sup>2</sup> = 0.92. <a href=\"https://github.com/ai-inventor-papers/ai-invention-8795ea-concepts-spread-once-adopters-make-them/tree/fork/run_kLBLH5WmvR9Y/round-3/experiment-7\">Code</a></p>\n497:    <p class=\"result-body\">Cheng et al.'s ideational consistency, rebuilt on OpenAlex for 12,311 concepts, reproduces their volume result: b = 0.428 (+53.5%/SD). Adding current volume collapses this to +1.3% [+0.5%, +2.1%]. The partial Spearman with rarefied breadth is negative, pooled with I<sup>2</sup> = 0 and all five groups negative. The consistency measure has Spearman +0.77 with edge persistence: a stable neighbourhood predicts growth but not breadth. <a href=\"https://github.com/ai-inventor-papers/ai-invention-8795ea-concepts-spread-once-adopters-make-them/tree/fork/run_kLBLH5WmvR9Y/round-5/experiment-14\">Code</a></p>\n503:    <p class=\"result-body\">On 3,188 DEV concepts, the breadth gap between the top and bottom O<sub>2r</sub> terciles decomposes as: early contact diversity 77.9%, frontier advance &minus;4.6%, retention 26.8%. On the held-out pool, the contact share is 0.633 [0.537, 0.727]. No discrete trajectory typology passes the naming rule; PCA reveals a continuum with PC1 (38.8% of variance) as a breadth axis. <a href=\"https://github.com/ai-inventor-papers/ai-invention-8795ea-concepts-spread-once-adopters-make-them/tree/fork/run_kLBLH5WmvR9Y/round-4/experiment-12\">Code</a></p>\n507:  <p>To address survivorship bias, 636 vocabulary-free phrase-born concepts (2003&ndash;2015 onsets) were tested. OPEN<sub>home</sub> gives PSP +0.117 [+0.020, +0.218] at control rung R3 for O<sub>2r</sub> (m = 30). The verdict is partial: the most demanding rung includes zero (+0.086 [&minus;0.009, +0.190]), and the signal is carried by neighbourhood novelty (NOV<sub>res</sub> +0.208 [+0.113, +0.303]). <a href=\"https://github.com/ai-inventor-papers/ai-invention-8795ea-concepts-spread-once-adopters-make-them/tree/fork/run_kLBLH5WmvR9Y/round-5/experiment-13\">Code</a></p>\n510:  <p>Four null models test whether the openness signal is an artefact (<a href=\"https://github.com/ai-inventor-papers/ai-invention-8795ea-concepts-spread-once-adopters-make-them/tree/fork/run_kLBLH5WmvR9Y/round-5/experiment-16\">code</a>). Subsampling to 10 home papers per year retains 68% of the association. A within-concept year-label permutation null absorbs the churn signal: excess NOVCHURN pooled PSP = +0.008 [&minus;0.02, +0.03] versus raw +0.116 [+0.09, +0.14]. The R<sup>2</sup> of raw persistence on the permutation-null mean is 0.66. What predicts breadth is a static property of the concept's home-topic partner mix, not temporal turnover.</p>\n511:  <p>A within-concept closure test (<a href=\"https://github.com/ai-inventor-papers/ai-invention-8795ea-concepts-spread-once-adopters-make-them/tree/fork/run_kLBLH5WmvR9Y/round-5/experiment-15\">code</a>) is null on the development set and opposite-signed on held-out (&minus;0.079 [&minus;0.146, &minus;0.013]). Early openness is a between-concept trait, not a within-concept mechanism. Temporal turnover is untested rather than refuted.</p>\n581:    <li><a href=\"https://github.com/ai-inventor-papers/ai-invention-8795ea-concepts-spread-once-adopters-make-them/tree/fork/run_kLBLH5WmvR9Y/round-1/experiment-1\">Does citing a concept &lsquo;as your own&rsquo; predict its spread?</a></li>\n582:    <li><a href=\"https://github.com/ai-inventor-papers/ai-invention-8795ea-concepts-spread-once-adopters-make-them/tree/fork/run_kLBLH5WmvR9Y/round-1/experiment-3\">Do diverse topic ties predict concept spread?</a></li>\n583:    <li><a href=\"https://github.com/ai-inventor-papers/ai-invention-8795ea-concepts-spread-once-adopters-make-them/tree/fork/run_kLBLH5WmvR9Y/round-1/experiment-4\">Where a concept lands early vs how broadly it spreads</a></li>\n584:    <li><a href=\"https://github.com/ai-inventor-papers/ai-invention-8795ea-concepts-spread-once-adopters-make-them/tree/fork/run_kLBLH5WmvR9Y/round-2/experiment-5\">Do hub fields keep new concepts?
